prompt: A region of 2D space that detects other `CollisionObject2D`s entering or exiting it.
explain: `Area2D` is a region of 2D space defined by one or multiple `CollisionShape2D` or `CollisionPolygon2D` child nodes. It detects when other `CollisionObject2D`s enter or exit it, and it also keeps track of which collision objects haven't exited it yet (i.e. which one are overlapping it).

prompt: Area2D: Returns a list of intersecting `Area2D`s. The overlapping area's `CollisionObject2D.collision_layer` must be part of this area's `CollisionObject2D.collision_mask` in order to be detected.
explain:
`get_overlapping_areas() -> Area2D[]`
Returns a list of intersecting `Area2D`s. The overlapping area's `CollisionObject2D.collision_layer` must be part of this area's `CollisionObject2D.collision_mask` in order to be detected.

prompt: Area2D: The rate at which objects stop spinning in this area. Represents the angular velocity lost per second.
explain:
`angular_damp: float = 1.0`
The rate at which objects stop spinning in this area. Represents the angular velocity lost per second.

prompt: Area2D: Emitted when the received `area` enters this area. Requires `monitoring` to be set to `true`.
explain:
`area_entered(area: Area2D)`
Emitted when the received `area` enters this area. Requires `monitoring` to be set to `true`.

prompt: Area2D: Returns a list of intersecting `PhysicsBody2D`s and `TileMap`s. The overlapping body's `CollisionObject2D.collision_layer` must be part of this area's `CollisionObject2D.collision_mask` in order to be detected.
explain:
`get_overlapping_bodies() -> Node2D[]`
Returns a list of intersecting `PhysicsBody2D`s and `TileMap`s. The overlapping body's `CollisionObject2D.collision_layer` must be part of this area's `CollisionObject2D.collision_mask` in order to be detected.

prompt: Area2D: Override mode for angular damping calculations within this area.
explain:
`angular_damp_space_override: int = 0`
Override mode for angular damping calculations within this area.

prompt: Area2D: Emitted when the received `area` exits this area. Requires `monitoring` to be set to `true`.
explain:
`area_exited(area: Area2D)`
Emitted when the received `area` exits this area. Requires `monitoring` to be set to `true`.

prompt: Area2D: Returns `true` if intersecting any `Area2D`s, otherwise returns `false`. The overlapping area's `CollisionObject2D.collision_layer` must be part of this area's `CollisionObject2D.collision_mask` in order to be detected.
explain:
`has_overlapping_areas() -> bool`
Returns `true` if intersecting any `Area2D`s, otherwise returns `false`. The overlapping area's `CollisionObject2D.collision_layer` must be part of this area's `CollisionObject2D.collision_mask` in order to be detected.

prompt: Area2D: The name of the area's audio bus.
explain:
`audio_bus_name: StringName = &"Master"`
The name of the area's audio bus.

prompt: Area2D: Emitted when a `Shape2D` of the received `area` enters a shape of this area. Requires `monitoring` to be set to `true`.
explain:
`area_shape_entered(area_rid: RID, area: Area2D, area_shape_index: int, local_shape_index: int)`
Emitted when a `Shape2D` of the received `area` enters a shape of this area. Requires `monitoring` to be set to `true`.

prompt: Area2D: Returns `true` if intersecting any `PhysicsBody2D`s or `TileMap`s, otherwise returns `false`. The overlapping body's `CollisionObject2D.collision_layer` must be part of this area's `CollisionObject2D.collision_mask` in order to be detected.
explain:
`has_overlapping_bodies() -> bool`
Returns `true` if intersecting any `PhysicsBody2D`s or `TileMap`s, otherwise returns `false`. The overlapping body's `CollisionObject2D.collision_layer` must be part of this area's `CollisionObject2D.collision_mask` in order to be detected.

prompt: Area2D: If `true`, the area's audio bus overrides the default audio bus.
explain:
`audio_bus_override: bool = false`
If `true`, the area's audio bus overrides the default audio bus.

prompt: Area2D: Emitted when a `Shape2D` of the received `area` exits a shape of this area. Requires `monitoring` to be set to `true`.
explain:
`area_shape_exited(area_rid: RID, area: Area2D, area_shape_index: int, local_shape_index: int)`
Emitted when a `Shape2D` of the received `area` exits a shape of this area. Requires `monitoring` to be set to `true`.

prompt: Area2D: Returns `true` if the given `Area2D` intersects or overlaps this `Area2D`, `false` otherwise. Note: The result of this test is not immediate after moving objects.
explain:
`overlaps_area(area: Node) -> bool`
Returns `true` if the given `Area2D` intersects or overlaps this `Area2D`, `false` otherwise. Note: The result of this test is not immediate after moving objects.

prompt: Area2D: The area's gravity intensity (in pixels per second squared). This value multiplies the gravity direction.
explain:
`gravity: float = 980.0`
The area's gravity intensity (in pixels per second squared). This value multiplies the gravity direction.

prompt: Area2D: Emitted when the received `body` enters this area. `body` can be a `PhysicsBody2D` or a `TileMap`.
explain:
`body_entered(body: Node2D)`
Emitted when the received `body` enters this area. `body` can be a `PhysicsBody2D` or a `TileMap`.

prompt: Area2D: Returns `true` if the given physics body intersects or overlaps this `Area2D`, `false` otherwise. Note: The result of this test is not immediate after moving objects.
explain:
`overlaps_body(body: Node) -> bool`
Returns `true` if the given physics body intersects or overlaps this `Area2D`, `false` otherwise. Note: The result of this test is not immediate after moving objects.

prompt: Area2D: The area's gravity vector (not normalized).
explain:
`gravity_direction: Vector2 = Vector2(0, 1)`
The area's gravity vector (not normalized).

prompt: Area2D: Emitted when the received `body` exits this area. `body` can be a `PhysicsBody2D` or a `TileMap`.
explain:
`body_exited(body: Node2D)`
Emitted when the received `body` exits this area. `body` can be a `PhysicsBody2D` or a `TileMap`.

prompt: Area2D: If `true`, gravity is calculated from a point (set via `gravity_point_center`). See also `gravity_space_override`.
explain:
`gravity_point: bool = false`
If `true`, gravity is calculated from a point (set via `gravity_point_center`). See also `gravity_space_override`.

prompt: Area2D: Emitted when a `Shape2D` of the received `body` enters a shape of this area. `body` can be a `PhysicsBody2D` or a `TileMap`.
explain:
`body_shape_entered(body_rid: RID, body: Node2D, body_shape_index: int, local_shape_index: int)`
Emitted when a `Shape2D` of the received `body` enters a shape of this area. `body` can be a `PhysicsBody2D` or a `TileMap`.

prompt: Area2D: If gravity is a point (see `gravity_point`), this will be the point of attraction.
explain:
`gravity_point_center: Vector2 = Vector2(0, 1)`
If gravity is a point (see `gravity_point`), this will be the point of attraction.

prompt: Area2D: Emitted when a `Shape2D` of the received `body` exits a shape of this area. `body` can be a `PhysicsBody2D` or a `TileMap`.
explain:
`body_shape_exited(body_rid: RID, body: Node2D, body_shape_index: int, local_shape_index: int)`
Emitted when a `Shape2D` of the received `body` exits a shape of this area. `body` can be a `PhysicsBody2D` or a `TileMap`.

prompt: A 2D physics body specialized for characters moved by script.
explain: `CharacterBody2D` is a specialized class for physics bodies that are meant to be user-controlled. They are not affected by physics at all, but they affect other physics bodies in their path.

prompt: CharacterBody2D: Allows to manually apply a snap to the floor regardless of the body's velocity. This function does nothing when `is_on_floor()` returns `true`.
explain:
`apply_floor_snap() -> void`
Allows to manually apply a snap to the floor regardless of the body's velocity. This function does nothing when `is_on_floor()` returns `true`.

prompt: CharacterBody2D: If `true`, the body will be able to move on the floor only. This option avoids to be able to walk on walls, it will however allow to slide down along them.
explain:
`floor_block_on_wall: bool = true`
If `true`, the body will be able to move on the floor only. This option avoids to be able to walk on walls, it will however allow to slide down along them.

prompt: CharacterBody2D: Returns the floor's collision angle at the last collision point according to `up_direction`, which is `Vector2.UP` by default. This value is always positive and only valid after calling `move_and_slide()` and when `is_on_floor()` returns `true`.
explain:
`get_floor_angle(up_direction: Vector2 = Vector2(0, -1)) -> float`
Returns the floor's collision angle at the last collision point according to `up_direction`, which is `Vector2.UP` by default. This value is always positive and only valid after calling `move_and_slide()` and when `is_on_floor()` returns `true`.

prompt: CharacterBody2D: If `false` (by default), the body will move faster on downward slopes and slower on upward slopes. If `true`, the body will always move at the same speed on the ground no matter the slope.
explain:
`floor_constant_speed: bool = false`
If `false` (by default), the body will move faster on downward slopes and slower on upward slopes. If `true`, the body will always move at the same speed on the ground no matter the slope.

prompt: CharacterBody2D: Returns the collision normal of the floor at the last collision point. Only valid after calling `move_and_slide()` and when `is_on_floor()` returns `true`.
explain:
`get_floor_normal() -> Vector2`
Returns the collision normal of the floor at the last collision point. Only valid after calling `move_and_slide()` and when `is_on_floor()` returns `true`.

prompt: CharacterBody2D: Maximum angle (in radians) where a slope is still considered a floor (or a ceiling), rather than a wall, when calling `move_and_slide()`. The default value equals 45 degrees.
explain:
`floor_max_angle: float = 0.7853982`
Maximum angle (in radians) where a slope is still considered a floor (or a ceiling), rather than a wall, when calling `move_and_slide()`. The default value equals 45 degrees.

prompt: CharacterBody2D: Returns the last motion applied to the `CharacterBody2D` during the last call to `move_and_slide()`. The movement can be split into multiple motions when sliding occurs, and this method return the last one, which is useful to retrieve the current direction of the movement.
explain:
`get_last_motion() -> Vector2`
Returns the last motion applied to the `CharacterBody2D` during the last call to `move_and_slide()`. The movement can be split into multiple motions when sliding occurs, and this method return the last one, which is useful to retrieve the current direction of the movement.

prompt: CharacterBody2D: Sets a snapping distance. When set to a value different from `0.0`, the body is kept attached to slopes when calling `move_and_slide()`.
explain:
`floor_snap_length: float = 1.0`
Sets a snapping distance. When set to a value different from `0.0`, the body is kept attached to slopes when calling `move_and_slide()`.

prompt: CharacterBody2D: Returns a `KinematicCollision2D` if a collision occurred. The returned value contains information about the latest collision that occurred during the last call to `move_and_slide()`.
explain:
`get_last_slide_collision() -> KinematicCollision2D`
Returns a `KinematicCollision2D` if a collision occurred. The returned value contains information about the latest collision that occurred during the last call to `move_and_slide()`.

prompt: CharacterBody2D: If `true`, the body will not slide on slopes when calling `move_and_slide()` when the body is standing still. If `false`, the body will slide on floor's slopes when `velocity` applies a downward force.
explain:
`floor_stop_on_slope: bool = true`
If `true`, the body will not slide on slopes when calling `move_and_slide()` when the body is standing still. If `false`, the body will slide on floor's slopes when `velocity` applies a downward force.

prompt: CharacterBody2D: Returns the linear velocity of the platform at the last collision point. Only valid after calling `move_and_slide()`.
explain:
`get_platform_velocity() -> Vector2`
Returns the linear velocity of the platform at the last collision point. Only valid after calling `move_and_slide()`.

prompt: CharacterBody2D: Maximum number of times the body can change direction before it stops when calling `move_and_slide()`. Must be greater than zero.
explain:
`max_slides: int = 4`
Maximum number of times the body can change direction before it stops when calling `move_and_slide()`. Must be greater than zero.

prompt: CharacterBody2D: Returns the travel (position delta) that occurred during the last call to `move_and_slide()`.
explain:
`get_position_delta() -> Vector2`
Returns the travel (position delta) that occurred during the last call to `move_and_slide()`.

prompt: CharacterBody2D: Sets the motion mode which defines the behavior of `move_and_slide()`.
explain:
`motion_mode: int = 0`
Sets the motion mode which defines the behavior of `move_and_slide()`.

prompt: CharacterBody2D: Returns the current real velocity since the last call to `move_and_slide()`. For example, when you climb a slope, you will move diagonally even though the velocity is horizontal.
explain:
`get_real_velocity() -> Vector2`
Returns the current real velocity since the last call to `move_and_slide()`. For example, when you climb a slope, you will move diagonally even though the velocity is horizontal.

prompt: CharacterBody2D: Collision layers that will be included for detecting floor bodies that will act as moving platforms to be followed by the `CharacterBody2D`. By default, all floor bodies are detected and propagate their velocity.
explain:
`platform_floor_layers: int = 4294967295`
Collision layers that will be included for detecting floor bodies that will act as moving platforms to be followed by the `CharacterBody2D`. By default, all floor bodies are detected and propagate their velocity.

prompt: CharacterBody2D: Returns a `KinematicCollision2D`, which contains information about a collision that occurred during the last call to `move_and_slide()`. Since the body can collide several times in a single call to `move_and_slide()`, you must specify the index of the collision in the range 0 to (`get_slide_collision_count()` - 1).
explain:
`get_slide_collision(slide_idx: int) -> KinematicCollision2D`
Returns a `KinematicCollision2D`, which contains information about a collision that occurred during the last call to `move_and_slide()`. Since the body can collide several times in a single call to `move_and_slide()`, you must specify the index of the collision in the range 0 to (`get_slide_collision_count()` - 1).

prompt: CharacterBody2D: Returns the number of times the body collided and changed direction during the last call to `move_and_slide()`.
explain:
`get_slide_collision_count() -> int`
Returns the number of times the body collided and changed direction during the last call to `move_and_slide()`.

prompt: Sprite node that contains multiple textures as frames to play for animation.
explain: `AnimatedSprite2D` is similar to the `Sprite2D` node, except it carries multiple textures as animation frames. Animations are created using a `SpriteFrames` resource, which allows you to import image files (or a folder containing said files) to provide the animation frames for the sprite.

prompt: AnimatedSprite2D: Returns the actual playing speed of current animation or `0` if not playing. This speed is the `speed_scale` property multiplied by `custom_speed` argument specified when calling the `play()` method.
explain:
`get_playing_speed() -> float`
Returns the actual playing speed of current animation or `0` if not playing. This speed is the `speed_scale` property multiplied by `custom_speed` argument specified when calling the `play()` method.

prompt: AnimatedSprite2D: The current animation from the `sprite_frames` resource. If this value is changed, the `frame` counter and the `frame_progress` are reset.
explain:
`animation: StringName = &"default"`
The current animation from the `sprite_frames` resource. If this value is changed, the `frame` counter and the `frame_progress` are reset.

prompt: AnimatedSprite2D: Emitted when `animation` changes.
explain:
`animation_changed()`
Emitted when `animation` changes.

prompt: AnimatedSprite2D: Returns `true` if an animation is currently playing (even if `speed_scale` and/or `custom_speed` are `0`).
explain:
`is_playing() -> bool`
Returns `true` if an animation is currently playing (even if `speed_scale` and/or `custom_speed` are `0`).

prompt: AnimatedSprite2D: The key of the animation to play when the scene loads.
explain:
`autoplay: String = ""`
The key of the animation to play when the scene loads.

prompt: AnimatedSprite2D: Emitted when the animation reaches the end, or the start if it is played in reverse. When the animation finishes, it pauses the playback.
explain:
`animation_finished()`
Emitted when the animation reaches the end, or the start if it is played in reverse. When the animation finishes, it pauses the playback.

prompt: AnimatedSprite2D: Pauses the currently playing animation. The `frame` and `frame_progress` will be kept and calling `play()` or `play_backwards()` without arguments will resume the animation from the current playback position.
explain:
`pause() -> void`
Pauses the currently playing animation. The `frame` and `frame_progress` will be kept and calling `play()` or `play_backwards()` without arguments will resume the animation from the current playback position.

prompt: AnimatedSprite2D: If `true`, texture will be centered. Note: For games with a pixel art aesthetic, textures may appear deformed when centered.
explain:
`centered: bool = true`
If `true`, texture will be centered. Note: For games with a pixel art aesthetic, textures may appear deformed when centered.

prompt: AnimatedSprite2D: Emitted when the animation loops.
explain:
`animation_looped()`
Emitted when the animation loops.

prompt: AnimatedSprite2D: Plays the animation with key `name`. If `custom_speed` is negative and `from_end` is `true`, the animation will play backwards (which is equivalent to calling `play_backwards()`).
explain:
`play(name: StringName = &"", custom_speed: float = 1.0, from_end: bool = false) -> void`
Plays the animation with key `name`. If `custom_speed` is negative and `from_end` is `true`, the animation will play backwards (which is equivalent to calling `play_backwards()`).

prompt: AnimatedSprite2D: If `true`, texture is flipped horizontally.
explain:
`flip_h: bool = false`
If `true`, texture is flipped horizontally.

prompt: AnimatedSprite2D: Emitted when `frame` changes.
explain:
`frame_changed()`
Emitted when `frame` changes.

prompt: AnimatedSprite2D: Plays the animation with key `name` in reverse. This method is a shorthand for `play()` with `custom_speed = -1.0` and `from_end = true`, so see its description for more information.
explain:
`play_backwards(name: StringName = &"") -> void`
Plays the animation with key `name` in reverse. This method is a shorthand for `play()` with `custom_speed = -1.0` and `from_end = true`, so see its description for more information.

prompt: AnimatedSprite2D: If `true`, texture is flipped vertically.
explain:
`flip_v: bool = false`
If `true`, texture is flipped vertically.

prompt: AnimatedSprite2D: Emitted when `sprite_frames` changes.
explain:
`sprite_frames_changed()`
Emitted when `sprite_frames` changes.

prompt: AnimatedSprite2D: Sets `frame` and `frame_progress` to the given values. Unlike setting `frame`, this method does not reset the `frame_progress` to `0.0` implicitly.
explain:
`set_frame_and_progress(frame: int, progress: float) -> void`
Sets `frame` and `frame_progress` to the given values. Unlike setting `frame`, this method does not reset the `frame_progress` to `0.0` implicitly.

prompt: AnimatedSprite2D: The displayed animation frame's index. Setting this property also resets `frame_progress`.
explain:
`frame: int = 0`
The displayed animation frame's index. Setting this property also resets `frame_progress`.

prompt: AnimatedSprite2D: Stops the currently playing animation. The animation position is reset to `0` and the `custom_speed` is reset to `1.0`.
explain:
`stop() -> void`
Stops the currently playing animation. The animation position is reset to `0` and the `custom_speed` is reset to `1.0`.

prompt: AnimatedSprite2D: The progress value between `0.0` and `1.0` until the current frame transitions to the next frame. If the animation is playing backwards, the value transitions from `1.0` to `0.0`.
explain:
`frame_progress: float = 0.0`
The progress value between `0.0` and `1.0` until the current frame transitions to the next frame. If the animation is playing backwards, the value transitions from `1.0` to `0.0`.

prompt: AnimatedSprite2D: The texture's drawing offset.
explain:
`offset: Vector2 = Vector2(0, 0)`
The texture's drawing offset.

explain: Sprite frame library for an `AnimatedSprite2D` or `AnimatedSprite3D` node. Contains frames and animation data for playback.

prompt: SpriteFrames: Adds a new `anim` animation to the library.
explain:
`add_animation(anim: StringName) -> void`
Adds a new `anim` animation to the library.

prompt: SpriteFrames: Adds a frame to the `anim` animation. If `at_position` is `-1`, the frame will be added to the end of the animation.

`add_frame(anim: StringName, texture: Texture2D, duration: float = 1.0, at_position: int = -1) -> void`

prompt: SpriteFrames: Removes all frames from the `anim` animation.
explain:
`clear(anim: StringName) -> void`
Removes all frames from the `anim` animation.

prompt: SpriteFrames: Removes all animations. An empty `default` animation will be created.
explain:
`clear_all() -> void`

prompt: SpriteFrames: Duplicates the animation `anim_from` to a new animation named `anim_to`. Fails if `anim_to` already exists, or if `anim_from` does not exist.

`duplicate_animation(anim_from: StringName, anim_to: StringName) -> void`
Duplicates the animation `anim_from` to a new animation named `anim_to`. Fails if `anim_to` already exists, or if `anim_from` does not exist.

prompt: SpriteFrames: Returns the loop mode for the `anim` animation.
explain:
`get_animation_loop_mode(anim: StringName) -> int`
Returns the loop mode for the `anim` animation.

prompt: SpriteFrames: Returns an array containing the names associated to each animation. Values are placed in alphabetical order.
explain:

Returns an array containing the names associated to each animation. Values are placed in alphabetical order.

prompt: SpriteFrames: Returns the speed in frames per second for the `anim` animation.
explain:
`get_animation_speed(anim: StringName) -> float`
Returns the speed in frames per second for the `anim` animation.

prompt: SpriteFrames: Returns the number of frames for the `anim` animation.

`get_frame_count(anim: StringName) -> int`

prompt: SpriteFrames: In this example, `playing_speed` refers to either `AnimatedSprite2D.get_playing_speed()` or `AnimatedSprite3D.get_playing_speed()`.

prompt: Animation: Adds a marker to this Animation.

`add_marker(name: StringName, time: float) -> void`

prompt: Animation: Returns `true` if the capture track is included. This is a cached readonly value for performance.
explain:
`capture_included: bool = false`

prompt: Animation: Adds a track to the Animation.
explain:
`add_track(type: int, at_position: int = -1) -> int`

prompt: Animation: The total length of the animation (in seconds). Note: Length is not delimited by the last key, as this one may be before or after the end to ensure correct interpolation and looping.
explain:
`length: float = 1.0`

prompt: Animation: The animation step value.

`step: float = 0.033333335`

prompt: Animation: Returns the start offset of the key identified by `key_idx`. The `track_idx` must be the index of an Audio Track.

`audio_track_get_key_start_offset(track_idx: int, key_idx: int) -> float`

`audio_track_get_key_stream(track_idx: int, key_idx: int) -> Resource`

prompt: Environment: The `Texture2D` or `Texture3D` lookup table (LUT) to use for the built-in post-process color grading. Can use a `GradientTexture1D` for a 1-dimensional LUT, or a `Texture3D` for a more complex LUT.
explain:
`adjustment_color_correction: Texture`
The `Texture2D` or `Texture3D` lookup table (LUT) to use for the built-in post-process color grading. Can use a `GradientTexture1D` for a 1-dimensional LUT, or a `Texture3D` for a more complex LUT.

prompt: Environment: Increasing `____` will make dark values darker and bright values brighter. This simple adjustment is applied to the rendered image after tonemaping.
explain:
`adjustment_contrast: float = 1.0`
Increasing `adjustment_contrast` will make dark values darker and bright values brighter. This simple adjustment is applied to the rendered image after tonemaping.

prompt: Environment: If `true`, enables the `adjustment_*` properties provided by this resource. If `false`, modifications to the `adjustment_*` properties will have no effect on the rendered scene.
explain:
`adjustment_enabled: bool = false`
If `true`, enables the `adjustment_*` properties provided by this resource. If `false`, modifications to the `adjustment_*` properties will have no effect on the rendered scene.

prompt: Environment: Applies a simple saturation adjustment to the rendered image after tonemaping. When `____` is set to `0.0`, the rendered image will be fully converted to a grayscale image.
explain:
`adjustment_saturation: float = 1.0`
Applies a simple saturation adjustment to the rendered image after tonemaping. When `adjustment_saturation` is set to `0.0`, the rendered image will be fully converted to a grayscale image.

prompt: Environment: The ambient light's `Color`. Only effective if `ambient_light_sky_contribution` is lower than `1.0` (exclusive).
explain:
`ambient_light_color: Color = Color(0, 0, 0, 1)`
The ambient light's `Color`. Only effective if `ambient_light_sky_contribution` is lower than `1.0` (exclusive).

prompt: Environment: The ambient light's energy. The higher the value, the stronger the light.
explain:
`ambient_light_energy: float = 1.0`
The ambient light's energy. The higher the value, the stronger the light.

prompt: Environment: Defines the amount of light that the sky brings on the scene. A value of `0.0` means that the sky's light emission has no effect on the scene illumination, thus all ambient illumination is provided by the ambient light.
explain:
`ambient_light_sky_contribution: float = 1.0`
Defines the amount of light that the sky brings on the scene. A value of `0.0` means that the sky's light emission has no effect on the scene illumination, thus all ambient illumination is provided by the ambient light.

prompt: Default environment properties for the entire scene (post-processing effects, lighting and background settings).
explain: The `WorldEnvironment` node is used to configure the default `Environment` for the scene. The parameters defined in the `WorldEnvironment` can be overridden by an `Environment` node set on the current `Camera3D`.

prompt: WorldEnvironment: The default `CameraAttributes` resource to use if none set on the `Camera3D`.
explain:
`camera_attributes: CameraAttributes`
The default `CameraAttributes` resource to use if none set on the `Camera3D`.

prompt: WorldEnvironment: The default `Compositor` resource to use if none set on the `Camera3D`.
explain:
`compositor: Compositor`
The default `Compositor` resource to use if none set on the `Camera3D`.

prompt: WorldEnvironment: The `Environment` resource used by this `WorldEnvironment`, defining the default properties.
explain:
`environment: Environment`
The `Environment` resource used by this `WorldEnvironment`, defining the default properties.

prompt: Directional light from a distance, as from the Sun.
explain: A directional light is a type of `Light3D` node that models an infinite number of parallel rays covering the entire scene. It is used for lights with strong intensity that are located far away from the scene to model sunlight or moonlight.

prompt: DirectionalLight3D: If `true`, shadow detail is sacrificed in exchange for smoother transitions between splits. Enabling shadow blend splitting also has a moderate performance cost.
explain:
`directional_shadow_blend_splits: bool = false`
If `true`, shadow detail is sacrificed in exchange for smoother transitions between splits. Enabling shadow blend splitting also has a moderate performance cost.

prompt: DirectionalLight3D: Proportion of `directional_shadow_max_distance` at which point the shadow starts to fade. At `directional_shadow_max_distance`, the shadow will disappear.
explain:
`directional_shadow_fade_start: float = 0.8`
Proportion of `directional_shadow_max_distance` at which point the shadow starts to fade. At `directional_shadow_max_distance`, the shadow will disappear.

prompt: DirectionalLight3D: The maximum distance for shadow splits. Increasing this value will make directional shadows visible from further away, at the cost of lower overall shadow detail and performance (since more objects need to be included in the directional shadow rendering).
explain:
`directional_shadow_max_distance: float = 100.0`
The maximum distance for shadow splits. Increasing this value will make directional shadows visible from further away, at the cost of lower overall shadow detail and performance (since more objects need to be included in the directional shadow rendering).

prompt: DirectionalLight3D: The light's shadow rendering algorithm.
explain:
`directional_shadow_mode: int = 2`
The light's shadow rendering algorithm.

prompt: DirectionalLight3D: Sets the size of the directional shadow pancake. The pancake offsets the start of the shadow's camera frustum to provide a higher effective depth resolution for the shadow.
explain:
`directional_shadow_pancake_size: float = 20.0`
Sets the size of the directional shadow pancake. The pancake offsets the start of the shadow's camera frustum to provide a higher effective depth resolution for the shadow.

prompt: DirectionalLight3D: The distance from camera to shadow split 1. Relative to `directional_shadow_max_distance`.
explain:
`directional_shadow_split_1: float = 0.1`
The distance from camera to shadow split 1. Relative to `directional_shadow_max_distance`.

prompt: DirectionalLight3D: The distance from shadow split 1 to split 2. Relative to `directional_shadow_max_distance`.
explain:
`directional_shadow_split_2: float = 0.2`
The distance from shadow split 1 to split 2. Relative to `directional_shadow_max_distance`.

prompt: DirectionalLight3D: The distance from shadow split 2 to split 3. Relative to `directional_shadow_max_distance`.
explain:
`directional_shadow_split_3: float = 0.5`
The distance from shadow split 2 to split 3. Relative to `directional_shadow_max_distance`.

prompt: A container that arranges its child controls horizontally.
explain: A variant of `BoxContainer` that can only arrange its child controls horizontally. Child controls are rearranged automatically when their minimum size changes.

prompt: A PBR (Physically Based Rendering) material to be used on 3D objects.
explain: `StandardMaterial3D`'s properties are inherited from `BaseMaterial3D`. `StandardMaterial3D` uses separate textures for ambient occlusion, roughness and metallic maps.

prompt: Abstract base class for input events.
explain: Abstract base class of all types of input events. See `Node._input()`.

prompt: InputEvent: Returns `true` if the given input event and this input event can be added together (only for events of type `InputEventMouseMotion`). The given input event's position, global position and speed will be copied.
explain:
`accumulate(with_event: InputEvent) -> bool`
Returns `true` if the given input event and this input event can be added together (only for events of type `InputEventMouseMotion`). The given input event's position, global position and speed will be copied.

prompt: InputEvent: The event's device ID. Note: `____` can be negative for special use cases that don't refer to devices physically present on the system.
explain:
`device: int = 0`
The event's device ID. Note: `device` can be negative for special use cases that don't refer to devices physically present on the system.

prompt: InputEvent: Returns a `String` representation of the event.
explain:
`as_text() -> String`
Returns a `String` representation of the event.

prompt: InputEvent: Returns a value between 0.0 and 1.0 depending on the given actions' state. Useful for getting the value of events of type `InputEventJoypadMotion`.
explain:
`get_action_strength(action: StringName, exact_match: bool = false) -> float`
Returns a value between 0.0 and 1.0 depending on the given actions' state. Useful for getting the value of events of type `InputEventJoypadMotion`.

prompt: InputEvent: Returns `true` if this input event matches a pre-defined action of any type. If `exact_match` is `false`, it ignores additional input modifiers for `InputEventKey` and `InputEventMouseButton` events, and the direction for `InputEventJoypadMotion` events.
explain:
`is_action(action: StringName, exact_match: bool = false) -> bool`
Returns `true` if this input event matches a pre-defined action of any type. If `exact_match` is `false`, it ignores additional input modifiers for `InputEventKey` and `InputEventMouseButton` events, and the direction for `InputEventJoypadMotion` events.

prompt: InputEvent: Returns `true` if the given action matches this event and is being pressed (and is not an echo event for `InputEventKey` events, unless `allow_echo` is `true`). Not relevant for events of type `InputEventMouseMotion` or `InputEventScreenDrag`.
explain:
`is_action_pressed(action: StringName, allow_echo: bool = false, exact_match: bool = false) -> bool`
Returns `true` if the given action matches this event and is being pressed (and is not an echo event for `InputEventKey` events, unless `allow_echo` is `true`). Not relevant for events of type `InputEventMouseMotion` or `InputEventScreenDrag`.

prompt: InputEvent: Returns `true` if the given action matches this event and is released (i.e. not pressed). Not relevant for events of type `InputEventMouseMotion` or `InputEventScreenDrag`.
explain:
`is_action_released(action: StringName, exact_match: bool = false) -> bool`
Returns `true` if the given action matches this event and is released (i.e. not pressed). Not relevant for events of type `InputEventMouseMotion` or `InputEventScreenDrag`.

prompt: InputEvent: Returns `true` if this input event's type is one that can be assigned to an input action: `InputEventKey`, `InputEventMouseButton`, `InputEventJoypadButton`, `InputEventJoypadMotion`, `InputEventAction`. Returns `false` for all other input event types.
explain:
`is_action_type() -> bool`
Returns `true` if this input event's type is one that can be assigned to an input action: `InputEventKey`, `InputEventMouseButton`, `InputEventJoypadButton`, `InputEventJoypadMotion`, `InputEventAction`. Returns `false` for all other input event types.

prompt: InputEvent: Returns `true` if this input event has been canceled.
explain:
`is_canceled() -> bool`
Returns `true` if this input event has been canceled.

prompt: InputEvent: Returns `true` if this input event is an echo event (only for events of type `InputEventKey`). An echo event is a repeated key event sent when the user is holding down the key.
explain:
`is_echo() -> bool`
Returns `true` if this input event is an echo event (only for events of type `InputEventKey`). An echo event is a repeated key event sent when the user is holding down the key.

prompt: InputEvent: Returns `true` if the specified `event` matches this event. Only valid for action events, which include key (`InputEventKey`), button (`InputEventMouseButton` or `InputEventJoypadButton`), axis `InputEventJoypadMotion`, and action (`InputEventAction`) events.
explain:
`is_match(event: InputEvent, exact_match: bool = true) -> bool`
Returns `true` if the specified `event` matches this event. Only valid for action events, which include key (`InputEventKey`), button (`InputEventMouseButton` or `InputEventJoypadButton`), axis `InputEventJoypadMotion`, and action (`InputEventAction`) events.

prompt: Defines a 3D environment's background by using a `Material`.
explain: The `Sky` class uses a `Material` to render a 3D environment's background and the light it emits by updating the reflection/radiance cubemaps.

prompt: A singleton for handling inputs.
explain: The `Input` singleton handles key presses, mouse buttons and movement, gamepads, and input actions. Actions and their events can be set in the Input Map tab in Project > Project Settings, or with the `InputMap` class.

prompt: Camera node, displays from a point of view.
explain: `Camera3D` is a special node that displays what is visible from its current location. Cameras register themselves in the nearest `Viewport` node (when ascending the tree).

prompt: A packed array of 32-bit floating-point values.
explain: An array specifically designed to hold 32-bit floating-point values (float). Packs data tightly, so it saves memory for large array sizes.

prompt: Generate an axis-aligned box `PrimitiveMesh`.
explain: Generate an axis-aligned box `PrimitiveMesh`. The box's UV layout is arranged in a 3×2 layout that allows texturing each face individually.

prompt: A built-in data structure that holds a sequence of elements.
explain: An array data structure that can contain a sequence of elements of any `Variant` type by default. Values can optionally be constrained to a specific type by creating a typed array.

prompt: A material that defines a simple sky for a `Sky` resource.
explain: `ProceduralSkyMaterial` provides a way to create an effective background quickly by defining procedural parameters for the sun, the sky and the ground. The sky and ground are defined by a main color, a color at the horizon, and an easing curve to interpolate between them.

prompt: A node used for animation playback.
explain: An animation player is used for general-purpose playback of animations. It contains a dictionary of `AnimationLibrary` resources and custom blend times between animation transitions.

prompt: Container for `Animation` resources.
explain: An animation library stores a set of animations accessible through `StringName` keys, for use with `AnimationPlayer` nodes.

prompt: A color transition.
explain: This resource describes a color transition by defining a set of colored points and how to interpolate between them. See also `Curve` which supports more complex easing methods, but does not support colors.

prompt: Represents a mouse or a pen movement.
explain: Stores information about a mouse or a pen motion. This includes relative position, absolute position, and velocity.

prompt: General-purpose sprite node.
explain: A node that displays a 2D texture. The texture displayed can be a region from a larger atlas texture, or a frame from a sprite sheet animation.

prompt: A GUI control that displays a `StyleBox`.
explain: `Panel` is a GUI control that displays a `StyleBox`. See also `PanelContainer`.

prompt: A 2D vector using integer coordinates.
explain: A 2-element structure that can be used to represent 2D grid coordinates or any other pair of integers. It uses integer coordinates and is therefore preferable to `Vector2` when exact precision is required.

prompt: A packed array of `Color`s.
explain: An array specifically designed to hold `Color`. Packs data tightly, so it saves memory for large array sizes.

prompt: Server for anything visible.
explain: The rendering server is the API backend for everything visible. The whole scene system mounts on it to display.

prompt: Provides access to common operating system functionalities.
explain: The `OS` class wraps the most common functionalities for communicating with the host operating system, such as the video driver, delays, environment variables, execution of binaries, command line, etc. Note: In Godot 4, `OS` functions related to window management, clipboard, and TTS were moved to the `DisplayServer` singleton (and the `Window` class). Functions related to time were removed and are only available in the `Time` class.

prompt: A 3×3 matrix for representing 3D rotation and scale.
explain: The `Basis` built-in `Variant` type is a 3×3 matrix used to represent 3D rotation, scale, and shear. It is frequently used within a `Transform3D`.

prompt: Camera node for 2D scenes.
explain: Camera node for 2D scenes. It forces the screen (current layer) to scroll following this node.

prompt: A horizontal slider that goes from left (min) to right (max).
explain: A horizontal slider, used to adjust a value by moving a grabber along a horizontal axis. It is a `Range`-based control and goes from left (min) to right (max).

prompt: A packed array of `Vector2`s.
explain: An array specifically designed to hold `Vector2`. Packs data tightly, so it saves memory for large array sizes.

prompt: Provides access to engine properties.
explain: The `Engine` singleton allows you to query and modify the project's run-time parameters, such as frames per second, time scale, and others. It also stores information about the current build of Godot, such as the current version.

prompt: Class representing a planar `PrimitiveMesh`.
explain: Class representing a planar `PrimitiveMesh`. This flat mesh does not have a thickness.

prompt: A node that provides a `Shape3D` to a `CollisionObject3D` parent.
explain: A node that provides a `Shape3D` to a `CollisionObject3D` parent and allows it to be edited. This can give a detection shape to an `Area3D` or turn a `PhysicsBody3D` into a solid object.

prompt: A button that brings up a dropdown with selectable options when pressed.
explain: `OptionButton` is a type of button that brings up a dropdown with selectable items when pressed. The item selected becomes the "current" item and is displayed as the button text.

prompt: A server interface for low-level window management.
explain: `DisplayServer` handles everything related to window management. It is separated from `OS` as a single operating system may support multiple display servers.

prompt: Class representing a spherical `PrimitiveMesh`.
explain: Class representing a spherical `PrimitiveMesh`.

prompt: Stores globally-accessible variables.
explain: Stores variables that can be accessed from everywhere. Use `get_setting()`, `set_setting()` or `has_setting()` to access them.

prompt: Represents a mouse button being pressed or released.
explain: Stores information about mouse click events. See `Node._input()`.

prompt: A 3D box shape used for physics collision.
explain: A 3D box shape, intended for use in physics. Usually used to provide a shape for a `CollisionShape3D`.

prompt: A built-in data structure that holds key-value pairs.
explain: Dictionaries are associative containers that contain values referenced by unique keys. Dictionaries will preserve the insertion order when adding new entries.

prompt: Abstract base class for viewports. Encapsulates drawing and interaction with a game world.
explain: A `Viewport` creates a different view into the screen, or a sub-view inside another viewport. Child 2D nodes will display on it, and child Camera3D 3D nodes will render on it too.

prompt: A 2D axis-aligned bounding box using floating-point coordinates.
explain: The `Rect2` built-in `Variant` type represents an axis-aligned rectangle in a 2D space. It is defined by its `position` and `size`, which are `Vector2`.

prompt: A 3D physics body that can't be moved by external forces. When moved manually, it doesn't affect other bodies in its path.
explain: A static 3D physics body. It can't be moved by external forces or contacts, but can be moved manually by other means such as code, `AnimationMixer`s (with `AnimationMixer.callback_mode_process` set to `AnimationMixer.ANIMATION_CALLBACK_MODE_PROCESS_PHYSICS`), and `RemoteTransform3D`.

prompt: A packed array of `String`s.
explain: An array specifically designed to hold `String`s. Packs data tightly, so it saves memory for large array sizes.

prompt: A container that keeps child controls in its center.
explain: `CenterContainer` is a container that keeps all of its child controls in its center at their minimum size.

prompt: A material defined by a custom `Shader` program and the values of its shader parameters.
explain: A material that uses a custom `Shader` program to render visual items (canvas items, meshes, skies, fog), or to process particles. Compared to other materials, `ShaderMaterial` gives deeper control over the generated shader code.

prompt: An interface to a game world that doesn't create a window or draw to the screen directly.
explain: `SubViewport` Isolates a rectangular region of a scene to be displayed independently. This can be used, for example, to display UI in 3D space.

prompt: A control for displaying text that can contain different font styles, images, and basic formatting.
explain: A control for displaying text that can contain custom fonts, images, and basic formatting. `RichTextLabel` manages these as an internal tag stack.

prompt: Base class for audio streams.
explain: Base class for audio streams. Audio streams are used for sound effects and music playback, and support WAV (via `AudioStreamWAV`), Ogg (via `AudioStreamOggVorbis`), and MP3 (via `AudioStreamMP3`) file formats.

prompt: An input field for single-line text.
explain: `LineEdit` provides an input field for editing a single line of text. - When the `LineEdit` control is focused using the keyboard arrow keys, it will only gain focus and not enter edit mode.

prompt: A shader implemented in the Godot shading language.
explain: A custom shader program implemented in the Godot shading language, saved with the `.gdshader` extension. This class is used by a `ShaderMaterial` and allows you to write your own custom behavior for rendering visual items or updating particle information.

prompt: A mathematical curve.
explain: This resource describes a mathematical curve by defining a set of points and tangents at each point. By default, it ranges between `0` and `1` on the X and Y axes, but these ranges can be changed.

prompt: A 2D texture that creates a pattern with colors obtained from a `Gradient`.
explain: A 2D texture that obtains colors from a `Gradient` to fill the texture data. This texture is able to transform a color transition into different patterns such as a linear or a radial gradient.

prompt: Omnidirectional light, such as a light bulb or a candle.
explain: An Omnidirectional light is a type of `Light3D` that emits light in all directions. The light is attenuated by distance and this attenuation can be configured by changing its energy, radius, and attenuation parameters.

prompt: A button that represents a binary choice.
explain: `CheckButton` is a toggle button displayed as a check field. It's similar to `CheckBox` in functionality, but it has a different appearance.

prompt: Virtual base class for applying visual properties to an object, such as color and roughness.
explain: `Material` is a base resource used for coloring and shading geometry. All materials inherit from it and almost all `VisualInstance3D` derived nodes carry a `Material`.

prompt: A packed array of bytes.
explain: An array specifically designed to hold bytes. Packs data tightly, so it saves memory for large array sizes.

prompt: A 3D physics body specialized for characters moved by script.
explain: `CharacterBody3D` is a specialized class for physics bodies that are meant to be user-controlled. They are not affected by physics at all, but they affect other physics bodies in their path.

prompt: A packed array of 32-bit integers.
explain: An array specifically designed to hold 32-bit integer values. Packs data tightly, so it saves memory for large array sizes.

prompt: A customizable `StyleBox` that doesn't use a texture.
explain: By configuring various properties of this style box, you can achieve many common looks without the need of a texture. This includes optionally rounded borders, antialiasing, shadows, and skew.

prompt: A horizontal line used for separating other controls.
explain: A horizontal separator used for separating other controls that are arranged vertically. `HSeparator` is purely visual and normally drawn as a `StyleBoxLine`.

prompt: The most important data type in Godot.
explain: In computer programming, a Variant class is a class that is designed to store a variety of other types. Dynamic programming languages like PHP, Lua, JavaScript and GDScript like to use them to store variables' data on the backend.

prompt: A singleton for working with time data.
explain: The Time singleton allows converting time between various formats and also getting time information from the system. This class conforms with as many of the ISO 8601 standards as possible.

prompt: A container that keeps its child controls within the area of a `StyleBox`.
explain: A container that keeps its child controls within the area of a `StyleBox`. Useful for giving controls an outline.

prompt: A button that represents a binary choice.
explain: `CheckBox` allows the user to choose one of only two possible options. It's similar to `CheckButton` in functionality, but it has a different appearance.

prompt: A container that arranges its child controls in a grid layout.
explain: `GridContainer` arranges its child controls in a grid layout. The number of columns is specified by the `columns` property, whereas the number of rows depends on how many are needed for the child controls.

prompt: Class representing a square mesh facing the camera.
explain: Class representing a square `PrimitiveMesh`. This flat mesh does not have a thickness.

prompt: Holds font source data and prerendered glyph cache, imported from a dynamic or a bitmap font.
explain: `FontFile` contains a set of glyphs to represent Unicode characters imported from a font file, as well as a cache of rasterized glyphs, and a set of fallback `Font`s to use. Use `FontVariation` to access specific OpenType variation of the font, create simulated bold / slanted version, and draw lines of text.

prompt: A 2D rectangle shape used for physics collision.
explain: A 2D rectangle shape, intended for use in physics. Usually used to provide a shape for a `CollisionShape2D`.

prompt: Holds physics-related properties of a surface, namely its roughness and bounciness.
explain: Holds physics-related properties of a surface, namely its roughness and bounciness. This class is used to apply these properties to a physics body.

prompt: A container that keeps a margin around its child controls.
explain: `MarginContainer` adds an adjustable margin on each side of its child controls. The margins are added around all children, not around each individual one.

prompt: A 2D circle shape used for physics collision.
explain: A 2D circle shape, intended for use in physics. Usually used to provide a shape for a `CollisionShape2D`.

prompt: The origin point in AR/VR.
explain: This is a special node within the AR/VR system that maps the physical location of the center of our tracking space to the virtual location within our game world. Multiple origin points can be added to the scene tree, but only one can used at a time.

prompt: A packed array of `Vector3`s.
explain: An array specifically designed to hold `Vector3`. Packs data tightly, so it saves memory for large array sizes.

prompt: A camera node which automatically positions itself based on XR tracking data.
explain: A camera node which automatically positions itself based on XR tracking data. In contrast to `XRController3D`, the render thread has access to more up-to-date tracking data, and the location of the `XRCamera3D` node can lag a few milliseconds behind what is used for rendering.

prompt: Server for AR and VR features.
explain: The AR/VR server is the heart of our Advanced and Virtual Reality solution and handles all the processing.

prompt: Node for 2D tile-based maps.
explain: Node for 2D tile-based maps. A `TileMapLayer` uses a `TileSet` which contain a list of tiles which are used to create grid-based maps.

prompt: Class representing a cylindrical `PrimitiveMesh`.
explain: Class representing a cylindrical `PrimitiveMesh`. This class can be used to create cones by setting either the `top_radius` or `bottom_radius` properties to `0.0`.

prompt: Tile library for tilemaps.
explain: A TileSet is a library of tiles for a `TileMapLayer`. A TileSet handles a list of `TileSetSource`, each of them storing a set of tiles.

prompt: A 3D physics body that is moved by a physics simulation.
explain: `RigidBody3D` implements full 3D physics. It cannot be controlled directly, instead, you must apply forces to it (gravity, impulses, etc.), and the physics simulation will calculate the resulting movement, rotation, react to collisions, and affect other physics bodies in its path.

prompt: A 3D capsule shape used for physics collision.
explain: A 3D capsule shape, intended for use in physics. Usually used to provide a shape for a `CollisionShape3D`.

prompt: A resource used for styling/skinning `Control`s and `Window`s.
explain: A resource used for styling/skinning `Control` and `Window` nodes. While individual controls can be styled using their local theme overrides (see `Control.add_theme_color_override()`), theme resources allow you to store and apply the same settings across all controls sharing the same type (e.g. style all `Button`s the same).

prompt: Base class for all other classes in the engine.
explain: An advanced `Variant` type. All classes in the engine inherit from Object.

prompt: A plane in Hessian normal form.
explain: Represents a normalized plane equation. `normal` is the normal of the plane (a, b, c normalized), and `d` is the distance from the origin to the plane (in the direction of "normal").

prompt: A 3D sphere shape used for physics collision.
explain: A 3D sphere shape, intended for use in physics. Usually used to provide a shape for a `CollisionShape3D`.

prompt: A region of 3D space that detects other `CollisionObject3D`s entering or exiting it.
explain: `Area3D` is a region of 3D space defined by one or multiple `CollisionShape3D` or `CollisionPolygon3D` child nodes. It detects when other `CollisionObject3D`s enter or exit it, and it also keeps track of which collision objects haven't exited it yet (i.e. which one are overlapping it).

prompt: A 3D node representing a spatially-tracked controller.
explain: This is a helper 3D node that is linked to the tracking of controllers. It also offers several handy passthroughs to the state of buttons and such on the controllers.

prompt: An input field for numbers.
explain: `SpinBox` is a numerical input text field. It allows entering integers and floating-point numbers.

prompt: A `Resource` that contains vertex array-based geometry.
explain: Mesh is a type of `Resource` that contains vertex array-based geometry, divided in surfaces. Each surface contains a completely separate array and a material used to draw it.

prompt: Server interface for low-level audio access.
explain: `AudioServer` is a low-level server interface for audio access. It is in charge of creating sample data (playable audio) as well as its playback via a voice interface.

prompt: A 3D axis-aligned bounding box.
explain: The `AABB` built-in `Variant` type represents an axis-aligned bounding box in a 3D space. It is defined by its `position` and `size`, which are `Vector3`.

prompt: A 1D texture that uses colors obtained from a `Gradient`.
explain: A 1D texture that obtains colors from a `Gradient` to fill the texture data. The texture is filled by sampling the gradient for each pixel.

prompt: A 2D physics body that can't be moved by external forces. When moved manually, it doesn't affect other bodies in its path.
explain: A static 2D physics body. It can't be moved by external forces or contacts, but can be moved manually by other means such as code, `AnimationMixer`s (with `AnimationMixer.callback_mode_process` set to `AnimationMixer.ANIMATION_CALLBACK_MODE_PROCESS_PHYSICS`), and `RemoteTransform2D`.

prompt: Base class for all windows, dialogs, and popups.
explain: A node that creates a window. The window can either be a native system window or embedded inside another `Window` (see `Viewport.gui_embed_subwindows`).

prompt: A node for displaying plain text in 3D space.
explain: A node for displaying plain text in 3D space. By adjusting various properties of this node, you can configure things such as the text's appearance and whether it always faces the camera.

prompt: A multiline text editor.
explain: A multiline text editor. It also has limited facilities for editing code, such as syntax highlighting support.

prompt: `Mesh` type that provides utility for constructing a surface from arrays.
explain: The `ArrayMesh` is used to construct a `Mesh` by specifying the attributes as arrays. The `MeshInstance3D` is ready to be added to the `SceneTree` to be shown.

prompt: A spotlight, such as a reflector spotlight or a lantern.
explain: A Spotlight is a type of `Light3D` node that emits lights in a specific direction, in the shape of a cone. The light is attenuated through the distance.

prompt: A material for `CanvasItem`s.
explain: `CanvasItemMaterial`s provide a means of modifying the textures associated with a CanvasItem. They specialize in describing blend and lighting behaviors for textures.

prompt: A handle for a `Resource`'s unique identifier.
explain: The RID `Variant` type is used to access a low-level resource by its unique ID. RIDs are opaque, which means they do not grant access to the resource by themselves.

prompt: Holds a particle configuration for `GPUParticles2D` or `GPUParticles3D` nodes.
explain: `ParticleProcessMaterial` defines particle properties and behavior. It is used in the `process_material` of the `GPUParticles2D` and `GPUParticles3D` nodes.

prompt: A node that provides a polygon shape to a `CollisionObject2D` parent.
explain: A node that provides a polygon shape to a `CollisionObject2D` parent and allows it to be edited. The polygon can be concave or convex.

prompt: A 2×3 matrix representing a 2D transformation.
explain: The `Transform2D` built-in `Variant` type is a 2×3 matrix representing a transformation in 2D space. It contains three `Vector2` values: `x`, `y`, and `origin`.

prompt: Generic 3D position hint for editing.
explain: Generic 3D position hint for editing. It's just like a plain `Node3D`, but it displays as a cross in the 3D editor at all times.

prompt: A built-in type for unique strings.
explain: `StringName`s are immutable strings designed for general-purpose representation of unique names (also called "string interning"). Two `StringName`s with the same value are the same object.

prompt: A container used for displaying the contents of a `SubViewport`.
explain: A container that displays the contents of underlying `SubViewport` child nodes. It uses the combined size of the `SubViewport`s as minimum size, unless `stretch` is enabled.

prompt: Lightweight object used for general-purpose animation via script, using `Tweener`s.
explain: Tweens are mostly useful for animations requiring a numerical property to be interpolated over a range of values. The name tween comes from in-betweening, an animation technique where you specify keyframes and the computer interpolates the frames that appear between them.

prompt: A button that represents a link.
explain: A button that represents a link. This type of button is primarily used for interactions that cause a context change (like linking to a web page).

prompt: A 3D world boundary (half-space) shape used for physics collision.
explain: A 3D world boundary shape, intended for use in physics. `WorldBoundaryShape3D` works like an infinite plane that forces all physics bodies to stay above it.

prompt: A 3D particle emitter.
explain: 3D particle node used to create a variety of particle systems and effects. `GPUParticles3D` features an emitter that generates some number of particles at a given rate.

prompt: ____ datatype.
explain: Native image datatype. Contains image data which can be converted to an `ImageTexture` and provides commonly used image processing methods.

prompt: Abstract base class for separators.
explain: Abstract base class for separators, used for separating other controls. `Separator`s are purely visual and normally drawn as a `StyleBoxLine`.

prompt: A 3D cylinder shape used for physics collision.
explain: A 3D cylinder shape, intended for use in physics. Usually used to provide a shape for a `CollisionShape3D`.

prompt: Represents a key on a keyboard being pressed or released.
explain: An input event for keys on a keyboard. Supports key presses, key releases and `echo` events.

prompt: A CPU-based 2D particle emitter.
explain: CPU-based 2D particle node used to create a variety of particle systems and effects. See also `GPUParticles2D`, which provides the same functionality with hardware acceleration, but may not run on older devices.

prompt: Node that projects a texture onto a `MeshInstance3D`.
explain: `Decal`s are used to project a texture onto a `Mesh` in the scene. Use Decals to add detail to a scene without affecting the underlying `Mesh`.

prompt: A container used to provide scrollbars to a child control when needed.
explain: A container used to provide a child control with scrollbars when needed. Scrollbars will automatically be drawn at the right (for vertical) or bottom (for horizontal) and will enable dragging to move the viewable Control (and its children) within the ScrollContainer.

prompt: Captures its surroundings to create fast, accurate reflections from a given point.
explain: Captures its surroundings as a cubemap, and stores versions of it with increasing levels of blur to simulate different material roughnesses. The `ReflectionProbe` is used to create high-quality reflections at a low performance cost (when `update_mode` is `UPDATE_ONCE`).

prompt: A 2D polyline that can optionally be textured.
explain: This node draws a 2D polyline, i.e. a shape consisting of several points connected by segments. `Line2D` is not a mathematical polyline, i.e. the segments are not infinitely thin.

prompt: Provides methods for file reading and writing operations.
explain: This class can be used to permanently store data in the user device's file system and to read from it. This is useful for storing game save data or player configuration files.

prompt: A button that brings up a `ColorPicker` when pressed.
explain: Encapsulates a `ColorPicker`, making it accessible by pressing a button. Pressing the button will toggle the `ColorPicker`'s visibility.

prompt: A 2D polygon.
explain: A Polygon2D is defined by a set of points. Each point is connected to the next, with the final point being connected to the first, resulting in a closed polygon.

prompt: A 1D texture where pixel brightness corresponds to points on a curve.
explain: A 1D texture where pixel brightness corresponds to points on a unit `Curve` resource, either in grayscale or in red. This visual representation simplifies the task of saving curves as image files.

prompt: Provides the content of a `Viewport` as a dynamic texture.
explain: A `ViewportTexture` provides the content of a `Viewport` as a dynamic `Texture2D`. This can be used to combine the rendering of `Control`, `Node2D` and `Node3D` nodes.

prompt: A `Texture2D` based on an `Image`.
explain: This way, textures can be created at run-time by loading images both from within the editor and externally. This is because images have to be imported as a `CompressedTexture2D` first to be loaded with `@GDScript.load()`.

prompt: Provides parameters for `PhysicsDirectSpaceState3D.intersect_ray()`.
explain: By changing various properties of this object, such as the ray position, you can configure the parameters for `PhysicsDirectSpaceState3D.intersect_ray()`.

prompt: A control used to show a set of internal `TreeItem`s in a hierarchical structure.
explain: A control used to show a set of internal `TreeItem`s in a hierarchical structure. The tree items can be selected, expanded and collapsed.

prompt: A base dialog used for user notification.
explain: The default use of `AcceptDialog` is to allow it to only be accepted or closed, with the same result. However, the `confirmed` and `canceled` signals allow to make the two actions different, and the `add_button()` method allows to add custom buttons and actions.

prompt: A vertical list of selectable items with one or multiple columns.
explain: This control provides a vertical list of selectable items that may be in a single or in multiple columns, with each item having options for text and an icon. Tooltips are supported and may be different for every item in the list.

prompt: A control used for visual representation of a percentage.
explain: A control used for visual representation of a percentage. Shows the fill percentage in the center.

prompt: Helper class for creating and parsing ____ data.
explain: The `JSON` class enables all data types to be converted to and from a JSON string. This is useful for serializing data, e.g. to save to a file or send over the network.

prompt: A texture that crops out part of another Texture2D.
explain: `Texture2D` resource that draws only part of its `atlas` texture, as defined by the `region`. An additional `margin` can also be set, which is useful for small adjustments.

prompt: Contains a `Curve3D` path for `PathFollow3D` nodes to follow.
explain: Can have `PathFollow3D` child nodes moving along the `Curve3D`. See `PathFollow3D` for more information on the usage.

prompt: Class representing a capsule-shaped `PrimitiveMesh`.
explain: Class representing a capsule-shaped `PrimitiveMesh`.

prompt: Describes a Bézier curve in 3D space.
explain: This class describes a Bézier curve in 3D space. It is mainly used to give a shape to a `Path3D`, but can be manually sampled for other purposes.

prompt: A node containing a bone hierarchy, used to create a 3D skeletal animation.
explain: `Skeleton3D` provides an interface for managing a hierarchy of bones, including pose, rest and animation (see `Animation`). It can also use ragdoll physics.

prompt: Used by the editor to extend its functionality.
explain: Plugins are used by the editor to extend functionality. The most common types of plugins are those which edit a given node or resource type, import plugins and export plugins.

prompt: A dialog for selecting files or directories in the filesystem.
explain: `FileDialog` is a preset dialog used to choose files and directories in the filesystem. It supports filter masks.

prompt: A CPU-based 3D particle emitter.
explain: CPU-based 3D particle node used to create a variety of particle systems and effects. See also `GPUParticles3D`, which provides the same functionality with hardware acceleration, but may not run on older devices.

prompt: A container that creates a tab for each child control, displaying only the active tab's control.
explain: Arranges child controls into a tabbed view, creating a tab for each one. The active tab's corresponding control is made visible, while all other child controls are hidden.

prompt: Texture-based button. Supports Pressed, Hover, Disabled and Focused states.
explain: `TextureButton` has the same functionality as `Button`, except it uses sprites instead of Godot's `Theme` resource. It is faster to create, but it doesn't support localization like more complex `Control`s.

prompt: Base class for all texture types.
explain: `Texture` is the base class for all texture types. Common texture types are `Texture2D` and `ImageTexture`.

prompt: A singleton for loading resource files.
explain: A singleton used to load resource files from the filesystem. It uses the many `ResourceFormatLoader` classes registered in the engine (either built-in or from a plugin) to load files into memory and convert them to a format that can be used by the engine.

prompt: A 3D trimesh shape used for physics collision.
explain: A 3D trimesh shape, intended for use in physics. Usually used to provide a shape for a `CollisionShape3D`.

prompt: A variation of a font with additional settings.
explain: Provides OpenType variations, simulated bold / slant, and additional font settings like OpenType features and extra spacing.

prompt: A container that arranges its child controls horizontally and wraps them around at the borders.
explain: A variant of `FlowContainer` that can only arrange its child controls horizontally, wrapping them around at the borders. This is similar to how text in a book wraps around when no more words can fit on a line.

prompt: Abstraction for working with modern low-level graphics APIs.
explain: `RenderingDevice` is an abstraction for working with modern low-level graphics APIs such as Vulkan. Compared to `RenderingServer` (which works with Godot's own rendering subsystems), `RenderingDevice` is much lower-level and allows working more directly with the underlying graphics APIs.

prompt: Provides a base class for different kinds of light nodes.
explain: Light3D is the abstract base class for light nodes. As it can't be instantiated, it shouldn't be used directly.

prompt: Abstract base class for fonts and font variations.
explain: Abstract base class for different font types. It has methods for drawing text and font character introspection.

prompt: A group of buttons that doesn't allow more than one button to be pressed at a time.
explain: A group of `BaseButton`-derived buttons. The buttons in a `ButtonGroup` are treated like radio buttons: No more than one button can be pressed at a time.

prompt: Generate a `PrimitiveMesh` from the text.
explain: Generate a `PrimitiveMesh` from the text. TextMesh can be generated only when using dynamic fonts with vector glyph contours.

prompt: A 2D particle emitter.
explain: 2D particle node used to create a variety of particle systems and effects. `GPUParticles2D` features an emitter that generates some number of particles at a given rate.

prompt: Base node for geometry-based visual instances.
explain: Base node for geometry-based visual instances. Shares some common functionality like visibility and custom materials.

prompt: Button for touch screen devices for gameplay use.
explain: TouchScreenButton allows you to create on-screen buttons for touch devices. It's intended for gameplay use, such as a unit you have to touch to move.

prompt: Manages the game loop via a hierarchy of nodes.
explain: As one of the most important classes, the `SceneTree` manages the hierarchy of nodes in a scene, as well as scenes themselves. Nodes can be added, fetched and removed.

prompt: A 4D vector using floating-point coordinates.
explain: A 4-element structure that can be used to represent 4D coordinates or any other quadruplet of numeric values. It uses floating-point coordinates.

prompt: A vertical line used for separating other controls.
explain: A vertical separator used for separating other controls that are arranged horizontally. `VSeparator` is purely visual and normally drawn as a `StyleBoxLine`.

prompt: Represents a screen drag event.
explain: Stores information about screen drag events. See `Node._input()`.

prompt: Represents a screen touch event.
explain: Stores information about multi-touch press/release input events. Supports touch press, touch release and `index` for multi-touch count and order.

prompt: Abstract base class for everything in 2D space.
explain: Abstract base class for everything in 2D space. Canvas items are laid out in a tree; children inherit and extend their parent's transform.

prompt: Class representing a prism-shaped `PrimitiveMesh`.
explain: Class representing a prism-shaped `PrimitiveMesh`.

prompt: Class representing a torus `PrimitiveMesh`.
explain: Class representing a torus `PrimitiveMesh`.

prompt: Describes a Bézier curve in 2D space.
explain: This class describes a Bézier curve in 2D space. It is mainly used to give a shape to a `Path2D`, but can be manually sampled for other purposes.

prompt: A material that defines a sky for a `Sky` resource by a set of physical properties.
explain: The `PhysicalSkyMaterial` uses the Preetham analytic daylight model to draw a sky based on physical properties. This results in a substantially more realistic sky than the `ProceduralSkyMaterial`, but it is slightly slower and less flexible.

prompt: Plays positional sound in 2D space.
explain: Plays audio that is attenuated with distance to the listener. By default, audio is heard from the screen center.

prompt: A node used for advanced animation transitions in an `AnimationPlayer`.
explain: A node used for advanced animation transitions in an `AnimationPlayer`. Note: When linked with an `AnimationPlayer`, several properties and methods of the corresponding `AnimationPlayer` will not function as expected.

prompt: A modal window used to display a list of options.
explain: `PopupMenu` is a modal window used to display a list of options. Useful for toolbars and context menus.

prompt: Abstract base class for 3D shapes used for physics collision.
explain: Abstract base class for all 3D shapes, intended for use in physics. Performance: Primitive shapes, especially `SphereShape3D`, are fast to check collisions against.

prompt: Base class for serializable objects.
explain: Resource is the base class for all Godot-specific resource types, serving primarily as data containers. Since they inherit from `RefCounted`, resources are reference-counted and freed when no longer in use.

prompt: A button that brings up a `PopupMenu` when clicked.
explain: A button that brings up a `PopupMenu` when clicked. To create new items inside this `PopupMenu`, use `get_popup().add_item("My Item Name")`.

prompt: A 3D vector using integer coordinates.
explain: A 3-element structure that can be used to represent 3D grid coordinates or any other triplet of integers. It uses integer coordinates and is therefore preferable to `Vector3` when exact precision is required.

prompt: Plays positional sound in 3D space.
explain: Plays audio with positional sound effects, based on the relative position of the audio listener. Positional effects include distance attenuation, directionality, and the Doppler effect.

prompt: Godot editor's interface.
explain: `EditorInterface` gives you control over Godot editor's window. It allows customizing the window, saving and (re-)loading scenes, rendering mesh previews, inspecting and editing resources and objects, and provides access to `EditorSettings`, `EditorFileSystem`, `EditorResourcePreview`, `ScriptEditor`, the editor viewport, and information about scenes.

prompt: A ray in 3D space, used to find the first collision object it intersects.
explain: A raycast represents a ray from its origin to its `target_position` that finds the closest object along its path, if it intersects any. `RayCast3D` can ignore some objects by adding them to an exception list, by making its detection reporting ignore `Area3D`s (`collide_with_areas`) or `PhysicsBody3D`s (`collide_with_bodies`), or by configuring physics layers.

prompt: A node used to create a parallax scrolling background.
explain: A ParallaxBackground uses one or more `ParallaxLayer` child nodes to create a parallax effect. Each `ParallaxLayer` can move at a different speed using `ParallaxLayer.motion_offset`.

prompt: Occludes light cast by a Light2D, casting shadows.
explain: Occludes light cast by a Light2D, casting shadows. The LightOccluder2D must be provided with an `OccluderPolygon2D` in order for the shadow to be computed.

prompt: Defines a 2D polygon for LightOccluder2D.
explain: Editor facility that helps you draw a 2D polygon used as resource for `LightOccluder2D`.

prompt: Wraps a pool of audio streams with pitch and volume shifting.
explain: Picks a random AudioStream from the pool, depending on the playback mode, and applies random pitch shifting and volume shifting during playback.

prompt: A material that provides a special texture to a `Sky`, usually an HDR panorama.
explain: A resource referenced in a `Sky` that is used to draw a background. `PanoramaSkyMaterial` functions similar to skyboxes in other engines, except it uses an equirectangular sky map instead of a `Cubemap`.

prompt: A container that splits two child controls horizontally and provides a grabber for adjusting the split ratio.
explain: A container that accepts only two child controls, then arranges them horizontally and creates a divisor between them. The divisor can be dragged around to change the size relation between the child controls.

prompt: Point sampler for a `Path3D`.
explain: This node takes its parent `Path3D`, and returns the coordinates of a point within it, given a distance from the first vertex. It is useful for making other nodes follow a path, without coding the movement pattern.

prompt: Positional 2D light source.
explain: Casts light in a 2D environment. This light's shape is defined by a (usually grayscale) texture.

prompt: The server responsible for language translations.
explain: The translation server is the API backend that manages all language translations. Translations are stored in `TranslationDomain`s, which can be accessed by name.

prompt: An input animation for an `AnimationNodeBlendTree`.
explain: A resource to add to an `AnimationNodeBlendTree`. Only has one output port using the `animation` property.

prompt: Exposes performance-related data.
explain: This class provides access to a number of different monitors related to performance, such as memory usage, draw calls, and FPS. These are the same as the values displayed in the Monitor tab in the editor's Debugger panel.

prompt: Shader uniform (used by `RenderingDevice`).
explain: This object is used by `RenderingDevice`.

prompt: Texture-based progress bar. Useful for loading screens and life or stamina bars.
explain: TextureProgressBar works like `ProgressBar`, but uses up to 3 textures instead of Godot's `Theme` resource. It can be used to create horizontal, vertical and radial progress bars.

prompt: Abstract base class for defining the 3D rendering properties of meshes.
explain: This class serves as a default material with a wide variety of rendering features and properties without the need to write shader code. See the tutorial below for details.

prompt: SPIR-V intermediate representation as part of an `RDShaderFile` (used by `RenderingDevice`).
explain: `RDShaderSPIRV` represents an `RDShaderFile`'s SPIR-V code for various shader stages, as well as possible compilation error messages. SPIR-V is a low-level intermediate shader representation.

prompt: A box-shaped 3D particle collision shape affecting `GPUParticles3D` nodes.
explain: A box-shaped 3D particle collision shape affecting `GPUParticles3D` nodes. Particle collision shapes work in real-time and can be moved, rotated and scaled during gameplay.

prompt: A parallax scrolling layer to be used with `ParallaxBackground`.
explain: A ParallaxLayer must be the child of a `ParallaxBackground` node. Each ParallaxLayer can be set to move at different speeds relative to the camera movement or the `ParallaxBackground.scroll_offset` value.

prompt: Texture with 3 dimensions, optionally compressed.
explain: `CompressedTexture3D` is the VRAM-compressed counterpart of `ImageTexture3D`. The file extension for `CompressedTexture3D` files is `.ctex3d`.

prompt: Base class for reference-counted objects.
explain: Base class for any object that keeps a reference count. `Resource` and many other helper objects inherit this class.

prompt: An empty `StyleBox` (does not display anything).
