explain: An empty `StyleBox` that can be used to display nothing instead of the default style (e.g. it can "disable" `focus` styles).

prompt: A built-in type representing a method or a standalone function.
explain: `Callable` is a built-in `Variant` type that represents a function. It can either be a method within an `Object` instance, or a custom callable used for different purposes (see `is_custom()`).

prompt: Provides common settings to customize the text in a `Label`.
explain: `LabelSettings` is a resource that provides common settings to customize the text in a `Label`. It will take priority over the properties defined in `Control.theme`.

prompt: A TCP server.
explain: A TCP server. Listens to connections on a port and returns a `StreamPeerTCP` when it gets an incoming connection.

prompt: A resource that holds all components of a 3D world, such as a visual scenario and a physics space.
explain: Class that has everything pertaining to a world: A physics space, a visual scenario, and a sound space. 3D nodes register their resources into the current 3D world.

prompt: A 3D convex polyhedron shape used for physics collision.
explain: A 3D convex polyhedron shape, intended for use in physics. Usually used to provide a shape for a `CollisionShape3D`.

prompt: Abstract base class for 2D game objects affected by physics.
explain: `PhysicsBody2D` is an abstract base class for 2D game objects affected by physics. All 2D physics bodies inherit from it.

prompt: A ray in 2D space, used to find the first collision object it intersects.
explain: A raycast represents a ray from its origin to its `target_position` that finds the closest object along its path, if it intersects any. `RayCast2D` can ignore some objects by adding them to an exception list, by making its detection reporting ignore `Area2D`s (`collide_with_areas`) or `PhysicsBody2D`s (`collide_with_bodies`), or by configuring physics layers.

prompt: A singleton for saving `Resource`s to the filesystem.
explain: A singleton for saving resource types to the filesystem. It uses the many `ResourceFormatSaver` classes registered in the engine (either built-in or from a plugin) to save resource data to text-based (e.g. `.tres` or `.tscn`) or binary files (e.g. `.res` or `.scn`).

prompt: This object contains all data related to a pose on a tracked object.
explain: XR runtimes often identify multiple locations on devices such as controllers that are spatially tracked. Orientation, location, linear velocity and angular velocity are all provided for each pose by the XR runtime.

prompt: Abstract base class for 3D game objects affected by physics.
explain: `PhysicsBody3D` is an abstract base class for 3D game objects affected by physics. All 3D physics bodies inherit from it.

prompt: A 3D shape that sweeps a region of space to detect `CollisionObject3D`s.
explain: Shape casting allows to detect collision objects by sweeping its `shape` along the cast direction determined by `target_position`. This is similar to `RayCast3D`, but it allows for sweeping a region of space, rather than just a straight line.

prompt: Internet protocol (____) support functions such as DNS resolution.
explain: IP contains support functions for the Internet Protocol (IP). TCP/IP support is in different classes (see `StreamPeerTCP` and `TCPServer`).

prompt: A 2D ray shape used for physics collision that tries to separate itself from any collider.
explain: A 2D ray shape, intended for use in physics. Usually used to provide a shape for a `CollisionShape2D`.

prompt: A tracked controller.
explain: An instance of this object represents a controller that is tracked. As controllers are turned on and the `XRInterface` detects them, instances of this object are automatically added to this list of active tracking objects accessible through the `XRServer`.

prompt: 2D sprite node in a 3D world.
explain: A node that displays a 2D texture in a 3D environment. The texture displayed can be a region from a larger atlas texture, or a frame from a sprite sheet animation.

prompt: Helper class to handle INI-style files.
explain: The stored data can be saved to or parsed from a file, though ConfigFile objects can also be used directly without accessing the filesystem. Any operation that mutates the ConfigFile such as `set_value()`, `clear()`, or `erase_section()`, only changes what is loaded in memory.

prompt: A font loaded from a system font. Falls back to a default theme font if not implemented on the host OS.
explain: `SystemFont` loads a font from a system font with the first matching name from `font_names`. It will attempt to match font style, but it's not guaranteed.

prompt: A server interface for low-level 3D navigation access.
explain: NavigationServer3D is the server that handles navigation maps, regions and agents. It does not handle A* navigation from `AStar3D`.

prompt: Computes and stores baked lightmaps for fast global illumination.
explain: The `LightmapGI` node is used to compute and store baked lightmaps. Lightmaps are used to provide high-quality indirect lighting with very little light leaking.

prompt: A 2D agent used to pathfind to a position while avoiding obstacles.
explain: A 2D agent used to pathfind to a position while avoiding static and dynamic obstacles. The calculation can be used by the parent node to dynamically move it along the path.

prompt: A 3D agent used to pathfind to a position while avoiding obstacles.
explain: A 3D agent used to pathfind to a position while avoiding static and dynamic obstacles. The calculation can be used by the parent node to dynamically move it along the path.

prompt: Contains baked lightmap and dynamic object probe data for `LightmapGI`.
explain: `LightmapGIData` contains baked lightmap and dynamic object probe data for `LightmapGI`. It is replaced every time lightmaps are baked in `LightmapGI`.

prompt: A unit of execution in a process.
explain: A unit of execution in a process. Can run methods on `Object`s simultaneously.

prompt: A physics joint that attaches two 2D physics bodies at a single point, allowing them to freely rotate.
explain: A physics joint that attaches two 2D physics bodies at a single point, allowing them to freely rotate. For example, a `RigidBody2D` can be attached to a `StaticBody2D` to create a pendulum or a seesaw.

prompt: A 3D physics body that can't be moved by external forces. When moved manually, it affects other bodies in its path.
explain: An animatable 3D physics body. It can't be moved by external forces or contacts, but can be moved manually by other means such as code, `AnimationMixer`s (with `AnimationMixer.callback_mode_process` set to `AnimationMixer.ANIMATION_CALLBACK_MODE_PROCESS_PHYSICS`), and `RemoteTransform3D`.

prompt: Provides direct access to a physics body in the `PhysicsServer2D`.
explain: Provides direct access to a physics body in the `PhysicsServer2D`, allowing safe changes to physics properties. This object is passed via the direct state callback of `RigidBody2D`, and is intended for changing the direct state of that body.

prompt: Provides methods for generating pseudo-random numbers.
explain: RandomNumberGenerator is a class for generating pseudo-random numbers. It currently uses PCG32.

prompt: A server interface for font management and text rendering.
explain: `TextServer` is the API backend for managing fonts and rendering text. Note: This is a low-level API, consider using `TextLine`, `TextParagraph`, and `Font` classes instead.

prompt: Provides direct access to a physics space in the `PhysicsServer2D`.
explain: Provides direct access to a physics space in the `PhysicsServer2D`. It's used mainly to do queries against objects and areas residing in a given space.

prompt: A unit quaternion used for representing 3D rotations.
explain: The `Quaternion` built-in `Variant` type is a 4D data structure that represents rotation in the form of a Hamilton convention quaternion. Compared to the `Basis` type which can store both rotation and scale, quaternions can only store rotation.

prompt: A container that splits two child controls vertically and provides a grabber for adjusting the split ratio.
explain: A container that accepts only two child controls, then arranges them vertically and creates a divisor between them. The divisor can be dragged around to change the size relation between the child controls.

prompt: A server interface for low-level 2D physics access.
explain: - A space is a self-contained world for a physics simulation. It contains bodies, areas, and joints.

prompt: An internal control for a single item inside `Tree`.
explain: A single item of a `Tree` control. It can contain other `TreeItem`s as children, which allows it to create a hierarchy.

prompt: A region that contributes to the default volumetric fog from the world environment.
explain: `FogVolume`s are used to add localized fog into the global volumetric fog effect. `FogVolume`s can also remove volumetric fog from specific areas if using a `FogMaterial` with a negative `FogMaterial.density`.

prompt: A server interface for low-level 3D physics access.
explain: - A space is a self-contained world for a physics simulation. It contains bodies, areas, and joints.

prompt: A container that arranges child controls horizontally or vertically and provides grabbers for adjusting the split ratios between them.
explain: A container that arranges child controls horizontally or vertically and creates grabbers between them. The grabbers can be dragged around to change the size relations between the child controls.

prompt: A material that controls how volumetric fog is rendered, to be assigned to a `FogVolume`.
explain: A `Material` resource that can be used by `FogVolume`s to draw volumetric effects. If you need more advanced effects, use a custom fog shader.

prompt: Base class for an XR interface implementation.
explain: This class needs to be implemented to make an AR or VR platform available to Godot and these should be implemented as C++ modules or GDExtension modules. Part of the interface is exposed to GDScript so you can detect, enable and configure an AR or VR platform.

prompt: A navigation mesh that defines traversable areas and obstacles.
explain: A navigation mesh is a collection of polygons that define which areas of an environment are traversable to aid agents in pathfinding through complicated spaces.

prompt: Stores audio data loaded from WAV files.
explain: AudioStreamWAV stores sound samples loaded from WAV files. To play the stored sound, use an `AudioStreamPlayer` (for non-positional audio) or `AudioStreamPlayer2D`/`AudioStreamPlayer3D` (for positional audio).

prompt: A 2D navigation mesh that describes a traversable surface for pathfinding.
explain: A navigation mesh can be created either by baking it with the help of the `NavigationServer2D`, or by adding vertices and convex polygon indices arrays manually. To bake a navigation mesh at least one outline needs to be added that defines the outer bounds of the baked area.

prompt: A physics joint that attaches two 3D physics bodies at a single point, allowing them to freely rotate.
explain: A physics joint that attaches two 3D physics bodies at a single point, allowing them to freely rotate. For example, a `RigidBody3D` can be attached to a `StaticBody3D` to create a pendulum or a seesaw.

prompt: A box-shaped region of 3D space that detects whether it is visible on screen.
explain: `VisibleOnScreenNotifier3D` represents a box-shaped region of 3D space. When any part of this region becomes visible on screen or in a `Camera3D`'s view, it will emit a `screen_entered` signal, and likewise it will emit a `screen_exited` signal when no part of it remains visible.

prompt: Texture with optional normal and specular maps for use in 2D rendering.
explain: `CanvasTexture` is an alternative to `ImageTexture` for 2D rendering. It allows using normal maps and specular maps in any node that inherits from `CanvasItem`.

prompt: A traversable 3D region that `NavigationAgent3D`s can use for pathfinding.
explain: A traversable 3D region based on a `NavigationMesh` that `NavigationAgent3D`s can use for pathfinding. Two regions can be connected to each other if they share a similar edge.

prompt: A stream peer that handles TCP connections.
explain: A stream peer that handles TCP connections. This object can be used to connect to TCP servers, or also is returned by a TCP server.

prompt: Represents a gamepad button being pressed or released.
explain: Input event type for gamepad buttons. For gamepad analog sticks and joysticks, see `InputEventJoypadMotion`.

prompt: A traversable 2D region that `NavigationAgent2D`s can use for pathfinding.
explain: A traversable 2D region based on a `NavigationPolygon` that `NavigationAgent2D`s can use for pathfinding. Two regions can be connected to each other if they share a similar edge.

prompt: Texture format (used by `RenderingDevice`).
explain: This object is used by `RenderingDevice`.

prompt: A time-scaling animation node used in `AnimationTree`.
explain: Allows to scale the speed of the animation (or reverse it) in any child `AnimationNode`s. Setting it to `0.0` will pause the animation.

prompt: Abstract base class for GUI buttons.
explain: `BaseButton` is an abstract base class for GUI buttons. It doesn't display anything by itself.

prompt: A node that applies a color tint to a canvas.
explain: `CanvasModulate` applies a color tint to all nodes on a canvas. Only one can be used to tint a canvas, but `CanvasLayer`s can be used to render things independently.

prompt: Mesh optimized for creating geometry manually.
explain: A mesh type optimized for creating geometry manually, similar to OpenGL 1.x immediate mode. Note: Generating complex geometries with `ImmediateMesh` is highly inefficient.

prompt: High-level multiplayer API interface.
explain: Base class for high-level multiplayer API implementations. See also `MultiplayerPeer`.

prompt: Texture view (used by `RenderingDevice`).
explain: This object is used by `RenderingDevice`.

prompt: ____ pushes its own `Transform3D` to another `Node3D` derived Node in the scene.
explain: RemoteTransform3D pushes its own `Transform3D` to another `Node3D` derived Node (called the remote node) in the scene. It can be set to update another Node's position, rotation and/or scale.

prompt: A sub-tree of many type `AnimationNode`s used for complex animations. Used by `AnimationTree`.
explain: This animation node may contain a sub-tree of any other type animation nodes, such as `AnimationNodeTransition`, `AnimationNodeBlend2`, `AnimationNodeBlend3`, `AnimationNodeOneShot`, etc. This is one of the most commonly used animation node roots. An `AnimationNodeOutput` node named `output` is created by default.

prompt: A native library for ____.
explain: The `GDExtension` resource type represents a shared library which can expand the functionality of the engine. The `GDExtensionManager` singleton is responsible for loading, reloading, and unloading `GDExtension` resources.

prompt: A physics joint that allows for complex movement and rotation between two 3D physics bodies.
explain: The `Generic6DOFJoint3D` (6 Degrees Of Freedom) joint allows for implementing custom types of joints by locking the rotation and translation of certain axes. The first 3 DOF represent the linear motion of the physics bodies and the last 3 DOF represent the angular motion of the physics bodies.

prompt: Base input event type for mouse events.
explain: Stores general information about mouse events.

prompt: Library of meshes.
explain: A library of meshes. Contains a list of `Mesh` resources, each with a name and ID.

prompt: Provides direct access to a physics body in the `PhysicsServer3D`.
explain: Provides direct access to a physics body in the `PhysicsServer3D`, allowing safe changes to physics properties. This object is passed via the direct state callback of `RigidBody3D`, and is intended for changing the direct state of that body.

prompt: Provides parameters for `PhysicsDirectSpaceState2D.intersect_ray()`.
explain: By changing various properties of this object, such as the ray position, you can configure the parameters for `PhysicsDirectSpaceState2D.intersect_ray()`.

prompt: A 2D axis-aligned bounding box using integer coordinates.
explain: The `Rect2i` built-in `Variant` type represents an axis-aligned rectangle in a 2D space, using integer coordinates. It is defined by its `position` and `size`, which are `Vector2i`.

prompt: Abstract base class for sliders.
explain: Abstract base class for sliders, used to adjust a value by moving a grabber along a horizontal or vertical axis. Sliders are `Range`-based controls.

prompt: Abstract base class for interacting with streams.
explain: StreamPeer is an abstract base class mostly used for stream-based protocols (such as TCP). It provides an API for sending and receiving data through streams as raw data or strings.

prompt: Node for 2D tile-based maps.
explain: Node for 2D tile-based maps. Tilemaps use a `TileSet` which contain a list of tiles which are used to create grid-based maps.

prompt: Exposes a 2D atlas texture as a set of tiles for a `TileSet` resource.
explain: An atlas is a grid of tiles laid out on a texture. Each tile in the grid must be exposed using `create_tile()`.

prompt: A tracked object.
explain: An instance of this object represents a device that is tracked, such as a controller or anchor point. HMDs aren't represented here as they are handled internally.

prompt: Registers a custom resource importer in the editor. Use the class to parse any file and import it as a new resource type.
explain: `EditorImportPlugin`s provide a way to extend the editor's resource import functionality. Use them to import resources from custom files or to provide alternatives to the editor's existing importers.

prompt: A 3D physics body that simulates the behavior of a car.
explain: This physics body implements all the physics logic needed to simulate a car. It is based on the raycast vehicle system commonly found in physics engines.

prompt: Loads a specific resource type from a file.
explain: Godot loads resources in the editor or in exported games using ResourceFormatLoaders. They are queried automatically via the `ResourceLoader` singleton, or when a resource with internal dependencies is loaded.

prompt: Base class for contextual windows and panels with fixed position.
explain: `Popup` is a base class for contextual windows and panels with fixed position. It's a modal by default (see `Window.popup_window`) and provides methods for implementing custom popup behavior.

prompt: A deformable 3D physics mesh.
explain: A deformable 3D physics mesh. Used to create elastic or deformable objects such as cloth, rubber, or other flexible materials.

prompt:
Application status indicator (aka notification area icon).
Note: Status indicator is implemented on macOS and Windows.
explain:
Application status indicator (aka notification area icon).
Note: Status indicator is implemented on macOS and Windows.

prompt: A 3D physics body for a `VehicleBody3D` that simulates the behavior of a wheel.
explain: A node used as a child of a `VehicleBody3D` parent to simulate the behavior of one of its wheels. This node also acts as a collider to detect if the wheel is touching a surface.

prompt: 2D sprite node in 3D world, that can use multiple 2D textures for animation.
explain: `AnimatedSprite3D` is similar to the `Sprite3D` node, except it carries multiple textures as animation `sprite_frames`. Animations are created using a `SpriteFrames` resource, which allows you to import image files (or a folder containing said files) to provide the animation frames for the sprite.

prompt: A dialog used for confirmation of actions.
explain: A dialog used for confirmation of actions. This window is similar to `AcceptDialog`, but pressing its Cancel button can have a different outcome from pressing the OK button.

prompt: Overrides the location sounds are heard from.
explain: Once added to the scene tree and enabled using `make_current()`, this node will override the location sounds are heard from. This can be used to listen from a location different from the `Camera3D`.

prompt: Provides occlusion culling for 3D nodes, which improves performance in closed areas.
explain: Occlusion culling can improve rendering performance in closed/semi-open areas by hiding geometry that is occluded by other objects. The occlusion culling system is mostly static.

prompt: This resource allows for creating a custom rendering effect.
explain: This resource defines a custom rendering effect that can be applied to `Viewport`s through the viewports' `Environment`. You can implement a callback that is called during rendering at a given stage of the rendering pipeline and allows you to insert additional passes.

prompt: A popup with a panel background.
explain: A popup with a configurable panel background. Any child controls added to this node will be stretched to fit the panel's size (similar to how `PanelContainer` works).

prompt: A 3D node that has its position automatically updated by the `XRServer`.
explain: This node can be bound to a specific pose of an `XRPositionalTracker` and will automatically have its `Node3D.transform` updated by the `XRServer`. Nodes of this type must be added as children of the `XROrigin3D` node.

prompt: Provides direct access to a physics space in the `PhysicsServer3D`.
explain: Provides direct access to a physics space in the `PhysicsServer3D`. It's used mainly to do queries against objects and areas residing in a given space.

prompt: Base class for resource importers.
explain: This is the base class for Godot's resource importers. To implement your own resource importers using editor plugins, see `EditorImportPlugin`.

prompt: A container that preserves the proportions of its child controls.
explain: A container type that arranges its child controls in a way that preserves their proportions automatically when the container is resized. Useful when a container has a dynamic size and the child nodes must adjust their sizes accordingly without losing their aspect ratios.

prompt: Node that can be the parent of `PhysicalBone3D` and can apply the simulation results to `Skeleton3D`.
explain: Node that can be the parent of `PhysicalBone3D` and can apply the simulation results to `Skeleton3D`.

prompt: A physics body used to make bones in a `Skeleton3D` react to physics.
explain: The `PhysicalBone3D` node is a physics body that can be used to make bones in a `Skeleton3D` react to physics. Note: In order to detect physical bones with raycasts, the `SkeletonModifier3D.active` property of the parent `PhysicalBoneSimulator3D` must be `true` and the `Skeleton3D`'s bone must be assigned to `PhysicalBone3D` correctly; it means that `get_bone_id()` should return a valid id (`>= 0`).

prompt: Base class for all GUI containers.
explain: Base class for all GUI containers. A `Container` automatically arranges its child controls in a certain way.

prompt: Real-time global illumination (GI) probe.
explain: `VoxelGI`s are used to provide high-quality real-time indirect light and reflections to scenes. They precompute the effect of objects that emit light and the effect of static geometry to simulate the behavior of complex light in real-time.

prompt: A singleton that manages all `InputEventAction`s.
explain: Manages all `InputEventAction` which can be created/modified from the project settings menu Project > Project Settings > Input Map or in code with `add_action()` and `action_add_event()`. See `Node._input()`.

prompt: A transition within an `AnimationNodeStateMachine` connecting two `AnimationRootNode`s.
explain: The path generated when using `AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback.travel()` is limited to the nodes connected by `AnimationNodeStateMachineTransition`. You can set the timing and conditions of the transition in detail.

prompt: Directional 2D light from a distance.
explain: A directional light is a type of `Light2D` node that models an infinite number of parallel rays covering the entire scene. It is used for lights with strong intensity that are located far away from the scene (for example: to model sunlight or moonlight).

prompt: Plays an animation once in an `AnimationNodeBlendTree`.
explain: A resource to add to an `AnimationNodeBlendTree`. This animation node will execute a sub-animation and return once it finishes.

prompt: A tracked hand in XR.
explain: A hand tracking system will create an instance of this object and add it to the `XRServer`. This tracking system will then obtain skeleton data, convert it to the Godot Humanoid hand skeleton and store this data on the `XRHandTracker` object.

prompt: A node used to rotate all bones of a `Skeleton3D` bone chain a way that places the end bone at a desired 3D position.
explain: SkeletonIK3D is used to rotate all bones of a `Skeleton3D` bone chain a way that places the end bone at a desired 3D position. A typical scenario for IK in games is to place a character's feet on the ground or a character's hands on a currently held object.

prompt: A 2D texture that supports drawing to itself via Blit calls.
explain: A 2D texture that can be modified via blit calls, copying from a target texture to itself. Primarily intended to be managed in code, a user must call `setup()` to initialize the state before drawing.

prompt: Abstract base class for 2D shapes used for physics collision.
explain: Abstract base class for all 2D shapes, intended for use in physics. Performance: Primitive shapes, especially `CircleShape2D`, are fast to check collisions against.

prompt: A class that stores an expression you can execute.
explain: An expression can be made of any arithmetic operation, built-in math function call, method call of a passed instance, or built-in type construction call. An example expression text using the built-in math functions could be `sqrt(pow(3, 2) + pow(4, 2))`.

prompt: Node used for displaying a `Mesh` in 2D.
explain: Node used for displaying a `Mesh` in 2D. This can be faster to render compared to displaying a `Sprite2D` node with large transparent areas, especially if the node takes up a lot of space on screen at high viewport resolutions.

prompt: Provides parameters for `PhysicsDirectSpaceState3D`'s methods.
explain: By changing various properties of this object, such as the shape, you can configure the parameters for `PhysicsDirectSpaceState3D`'s methods.

prompt: Saves a specific resource type to a file.
explain: The engine can save resources when you do it from the editor, or when you use the `ResourceSaver` singleton. This is accomplished thanks to multiple `ResourceFormatSaver`s, each handling its own format and called automatically by the engine.

prompt: A node that may modify a Skeleton3D's bones.
explain: `SkeletonModifier3D` retrieves a target `Skeleton3D` by having a `Skeleton3D` parent. If there is an `AnimationMixer`, a modification always performs after playback process of the `AnimationMixer`.

prompt: A rectangular region of 2D space that, when visible on screen, enables a target node.
explain: `VisibleOnScreenEnabler2D` contains a rectangular region of 2D space and a target node. The target node will be automatically enabled (via its `Node.process_mode` property) when any part of this region becomes visible on the screen, and automatically disabled otherwise.

prompt: A state machine with multiple `AnimationRootNode`s, used by `AnimationTree`.
explain: Contains multiple `AnimationRootNode`s representing animation states, connected in a graph. State transitions can be configured to happen automatically or via code, using a shortest-path algorithm.

prompt: Provides playback control for an `AnimationNodeStateMachine`.
explain: Allows control of `AnimationTree` state machines created with `AnimationNodeStateMachine`. Retrieve with `$AnimationTree.get("parameters/playback")`.

prompt: Boolean matrix.
explain: A two-dimensional array of boolean values, can be used to efficiently store a binary matrix (every matrix element takes only one bit) and query the values using natural cartesian coordinates.

prompt: Stores attributes used to customize how a Viewport is rendered.
explain: The compositor resource stores attributes used to customize how a `Viewport` is rendered.

prompt: Abstract render data object, holds frame data related to rendering a single frame of a viewport.
explain: Abstract render data object, exists for the duration of rendering a single viewport. See also `RenderDataRD`, `RenderSceneData`, and `RenderSceneDataRD`.

prompt: TLS configuration for clients and servers.
explain: TLSOptions abstracts the configuration options for the `StreamPeerTLS` and `PacketPeerDTLS` classes. Objects of this class cannot be instantiated directly, and one of the static methods `client()`, `client_unsafe()`, or `server()` should be used instead.

prompt: Texture for 2D that is bound to a texture created on the `RenderingDevice`.
explain: This texture class allows you to use a 2D texture created directly on the `RenderingDevice` as a texture for materials, meshes, etc. Note: `Texture2DRD` is intended for low-level usage with `RenderingDevice`. For most use cases, use `Texture2D` instead.

prompt: A language translation that maps a collection of strings to their individual translations.
explain: `Translation` maps a collection of strings to their individual translations, and also provides convenience methods for pluralization. A `Translation` consists of messages.

prompt: Uniform set cache manager for Rendering Device based renderers.
explain: Uniform set cache manager for `RenderingDevice`-based renderers. Provides a way to create a uniform set and reuse it in subsequent calls for as long as the uniform set exists.

prompt: A 2D world boundary (half-plane) shape used for physics collision.
explain: A 2D world boundary shape, intended for use in physics. `WorldBoundaryShape2D` works like an infinite straight line that forces all physics bodies to stay above it.

prompt: The parent of a hierarchy of `Bone2D`s, used to create a 2D skeletal animation.
explain: `Skeleton2D` parents a hierarchy of `Bone2D` nodes. It holds a reference to each `Bone2D`'s rest pose and acts as a single point of access to its bones.

prompt: An area light, such as a neon light tube or a screen.
explain: An area light is a type of `Light3D` node that emits light over a two-dimensional area, in the shape of a rectangle. The light is attenuated throughout the distance.

prompt: A joint used with `Skeleton2D` to control and animate other nodes.
explain: A hierarchy of `Bone2D`s can be bound to a `Skeleton2D` to control and animate other `Node2D` nodes. You can use `Bone2D` and `Skeleton2D` nodes to animate 2D meshes created with the `Polygon2D` UV editor.

prompt: A container that can be expanded/collapsed.
explain: A container that can be expanded/collapsed, with a title that can be filled with controls, such as buttons. This is also called an accordion.

prompt: A server interface for low-level 2D navigation access.
explain: NavigationServer2D is the server that handles navigation maps, regions and agents. It does not handle A* navigation from `AStar2D` or `AStarGrid2D`.

prompt: Blends two animations linearly inside of an `AnimationNodeBlendTree`.
explain: A resource to add to an `AnimationNodeBlendTree`. Blends two animations linearly based on the amount value.

prompt: A spheroid-shaped attractor that influences particles from `GPUParticles3D` nodes.
explain: A spheroid-shaped attractor that influences particles from `GPUParticles3D` nodes. Can be used to attract particles towards its origin, or to push them away from its origin.

prompt: An editor for graph-like structures, using `GraphNode`s.
explain: `GraphEdit` provides tools for creation, manipulation, and display of various graphs. Its main purpose in the engine is to power the visual programming systems, such as visual shaders, but it is also available for use in user projects.

prompt: Helper tool to create geometry.
explain: The above `SurfaceTool` now contains one vertex of a triangle which has a UV coordinate and a specified `Color`. If another vertex were added without calling `set_uv()` or `set_color()`, then the last values would be used.

prompt: An implementation of A* for finding the shortest path between two points on a partial 2D grid.
explain: `AStarGrid2D` is a variant of `AStar2D` that is specialized for partial 2D grids. It is simpler to use because it doesn't require you to manually create points and connect them together.

prompt: A multiline text editor designed for editing code.
explain: CodeEdit is a specialized `TextEdit` designed for editing plain text code files. It has many features commonly found in code editors such as line numbers, line folding, code completion, indent management, and string/comment management.

prompt: A group of foldable containers that doesn't allow more than one container to be expanded at a time.
explain: A group of `FoldableContainer`-derived nodes. Only one container can be expanded at a time.

prompt: ____ is a special `GraphElement` that can be used to organize other `GraphElement`s inside a `GraphEdit`.
explain: GraphFrame is a special `GraphElement` to which other `GraphElement`s can be attached. It can be configured to automatically resize to enclose all attached `GraphElement`s.

prompt: A stream peer that handles TLS connections.
explain: A stream peer that handles TLS connections. This object can be used to connect to a TLS server or accept a single TLS client connection.

prompt: A node for driving hand meshes from `XRHandTracker` data.
explain: This node uses hand tracking data from an `XRHandTracker` to pose the skeleton of a hand mesh. Positioning of hands is performed by creating an `XRNode3D` ancestor of the hand mesh driven by the same `XRHandTracker`.

prompt: A container with connection ports, representing a node in a `GraphEdit`.
explain: `GraphNode` allows to create nodes for a `GraphEdit` graph with customizable content based on its child controls. `GraphNode` is derived from `Container` and it is responsible for placing its children on screen.

prompt: Represents axis motions (such as joystick or analog triggers) from a gamepad.
explain: Stores information about joystick motions. One `InputEventJoypadMotion` represents one axis at a time.

prompt: Represents a MIDI message from a MIDI device, such as a musical keyboard.
explain: InputEventMIDI stores information about messages from MIDI (Musical Instrument Digital Interface) devices. These may include musical keyboards, synthesizers, and drum machines.

prompt: Abstract base class for all 2D physics joints.
explain: Abstract base class for all joints in 2D physics. 2D joints bind together two physics bodies (`node_a` and `node_b`) and apply a constraint.

prompt: Abstract base class for all 3D physics joints.
explain: Abstract base class for all joints in 3D physics. 3D joints bind together two physics bodies (`node_a` and `node_b`) and apply a constraint.

prompt: Container for parsed source geometry data used in navigation mesh baking.
explain: Container for parsed source geometry data used in navigation mesh baking.

prompt: Container for parsed source geometry data used in navigation mesh baking.
explain: Container for parsed source geometry data used in navigation mesh baking.

prompt: Abstract class for all Tweeners used by `Tween`.
explain: Tweeners are objects that perform a specific animating task, e.g. interpolating a property or calling a method at a given time. A `Tweener` can't be created manually, you need to use a dedicated method from `Tween`.

prompt: Physically-based camera settings.
explain: `CameraAttributesPhysical` is used to set rendering settings based on a physically-based camera's settings. It is responsible for exposure, auto-exposure, and depth of field.

prompt: A physics joint that connects two 2D physics bodies with a spring-like force.
explain: A physics joint that connects two 2D physics bodies with a spring-like force. This behaves like a spring that always wants to stretch to a given length.

prompt: Provides methods for managing directories and their content.
explain: This class is used to manage directories and their content, even outside of the project folder. `DirAccess` can't be instantiated directly.

prompt: A real-time heightmap-shaped 3D particle collision shape affecting `GPUParticles3D` nodes.
explain: A real-time heightmap-shaped 3D particle collision shape affecting `GPUParticles3D` nodes. Heightmap shapes allow for efficiently representing collisions for convex and concave objects with a single "floor" (such as terrain).

prompt: A baked signed distance field 3D particle collision shape affecting `GPUParticles3D` nodes.
explain: A baked signed distance field 3D particle collision shape affecting `GPUParticles3D` nodes. Signed distance fields (SDF) allow for efficiently representing approximate collision shapes for convex and concave objects of any shape.

prompt: A sphere-shaped 3D particle collision shape affecting `GPUParticles3D` nodes.
explain: A sphere-shaped 3D particle collision shape affecting `GPUParticles3D` nodes. Particle collision shapes work in real-time and can be moved, rotated and scaled during gameplay.

prompt: A physics joint that restricts the movement of two 2D physics bodies to a fixed axis.
explain: A physics joint that restricts the movement of two 2D physics bodies to a fixed axis. For example, a `StaticBody2D` representing a piston base can be attached to a `RigidBody2D` representing the piston head, moving up and down.

prompt: Abstract class for specialized `PacketPeer`s used by the `MultiplayerAPI`.
explain: Manages the connection with one or more remote peers acting as server or client and assigning unique IDs to each of them. See also `MultiplayerAPI`.

prompt: Provides parameters for `PhysicsDirectSpaceState2D`'s methods.
explain: By changing various properties of this object, such as the shape, you can configure the parameters for `PhysicsDirectSpaceState2D`'s methods.

prompt: Sampler state (used by `RenderingDevice`).
explain: This object is used by `RenderingDevice`.

prompt: A singleton for managing `TextServer` implementations.
explain: `TextServerManager` is the API backend for loading, enumerating, and switching `TextServer`s. Note: Switching text server at runtime is possible, but will invalidate all fonts and text buffers.

prompt: Represents a straight tube-shaped `PrimitiveMesh` with variable width.
explain: `TubeTrailMesh` represents a straight tube-shaped mesh with variable width. The tube is composed of a number of cylindrical sections, each with the same `section_length` and number of `section_rings`.

prompt: A vertical slider that goes from bottom (min) to top (max).
explain: A vertical slider, used to adjust a value by moving a grabber along a vertical axis. It is a `Range`-based control and goes from bottom (min) to top (max).

prompt: A singleton that allocates some `Thread`s on startup, used to offload tasks to these threads.
explain: The `WorkerThreadPool` singleton allocates a set of `Thread`s (called worker threads) on project startup and provides methods for offloading tasks to them. This can be used for simple multithreading without having to create `Thread`s.

prompt: A 2D physics body that can't be moved by external forces. When moved manually, it affects other bodies in its path.
explain: An animatable 2D physics body. It can't be moved by external forces or contacts, but can be moved manually by other means such as code, `AnimationMixer`s (with `AnimationMixer.callback_mode_process` set to `AnimationMixer.ANIMATION_CALLBACK_MODE_PROCESS_PHYSICS`), and `RemoteTransform2D`.

prompt: A transition within an `AnimationTree` connecting two `AnimationNode`s.
explain: Simple state machine for cases which don't require a more advanced `AnimationNodeStateMachine`. Animations can be connected to the inputs and transition times can be specified.

prompt: 3D polygon shape for use with occlusion culling in `OccluderInstance3D`.
explain: `ArrayOccluder3D` stores an arbitrary 3D polygon shape that can be used by the engine's occlusion culling system. This is analogous to `ArrayMesh`, but for occluders.

prompt: Base class for audio effect resources.
explain: The base `Resource` for every audio effect. In the editor, an audio effect can be added to the current bus layout through the Audio panel.

prompt: Queryable instance of an `AudioEffectSpectrumAnalyzer`.
explain: The runtime part of an `AudioEffectSpectrumAnalyzer`, which can be used to query the magnitude of a frequency range on its host bus. An instance of this class can be obtained with `AudioServer.get_bus_effect_instance()`.

prompt: An audio stream with utilities for procedural sound generation.
explain: `AudioStreamGenerator` is a type of audio stream that does not play back sounds on its own; instead, it expects a script to generate audio data for it. See also `AudioStreamGeneratorPlayback`.

prompt: Plays real-time audio input data.
explain: When used directly in an `AudioStreamPlayer` node, `AudioStreamMicrophone` plays back microphone input in real-time. This can be used in conjunction with `AudioEffectCapture` to process the data or save it.

prompt: Meta class for playing back audio.
explain: Can play, loop, pause a scroll through audio. See `AudioStream` and `AudioStreamOggVorbis` for usage.

prompt: А node that dynamically copies or overrides the 3D transform of a bone in its parent `Skeleton3D`.
explain: This node selects a bone in a `Skeleton3D` and attaches to it. This means that the `BoneAttachment3D` node will either dynamically copy or override the 3D transform of the selected bone.

prompt: Cuboid shape for use with occlusion culling in `OccluderInstance3D`.
explain: `BoxOccluder3D` stores a cuboid shape that can be used by the engine's occlusion culling system. See `OccluderInstance3D`'s documentation for instructions on setting up occlusion culling.

prompt: Parent class for camera settings.
explain: Controls camera-specific attributes such as depth of field and exposure override. When used in a `WorldEnvironment` it provides default settings for exposure, auto-exposure, and depth of field that will be used by all cameras without their own `CameraAttributes`, including the editor camera.

prompt: Camera settings in an easy to use format.
explain: Controls camera-specific attributes such as auto-exposure, depth of field, and exposure override. When used in a `WorldEnvironment` it provides default settings for exposure, auto-exposure, and depth of field that will be used by all cameras without their own `CameraAttributes`, including the editor camera.

prompt: A class information repository.
explain: Provides access to metadata stored for every available engine class. Note: Script-defined classes with `class_name` are not part of `ClassDB`, so they will not return reflection data such as a method or property list.

prompt: A syntax highlighter intended for code.
explain: By adjusting various properties of this resource, you can change the colors of strings, comments, numbers, and other text patterns inside a `TextEdit` control.

prompt: An optionally compressed `Cubemap`.
explain: - Lossless (WebP or PNG, uncompressed on the GPU) - Lossy (WebP, uncompressed on the GPU) - VRAM Compressed (compressed on the GPU) - VRAM Uncompressed (uncompressed on the GPU) - Basis Universal (compressed on the GPU. Lower file sizes than VRAM Compressed, but slower to compress and lower quality than VRAM Compressed) Only VRAM Compressed actually reduces the memory usage on the GPU.

prompt: Texture with 2 dimensions, optionally compressed.
explain: - Lossless (WebP or PNG, uncompressed on the GPU) - Lossy (WebP, uncompressed on the GPU) - VRAM Compressed (compressed on the GPU) - VRAM Uncompressed (uncompressed on the GPU) - Basis Universal (compressed on the GPU. Lower file sizes than VRAM Compressed, but slower to compress and lower quality than VRAM Compressed) Only VRAM Compressed actually reduces the memory usage on the GPU.

prompt: A 2D polyline shape used for physics collision.
explain: A 2D polyline shape, intended for use in physics. Used internally in `CollisionPolygon2D` when it's in `CollisionPolygon2D.BUILD_SEGMENTS` mode.

prompt: A physics joint that connects two 3D physics bodies in a way that simulates a ball-and-socket joint.
explain: A physics joint that connects two 3D physics bodies in a way that simulates a ball-and-socket joint. The twist axis is initiated as the X axis of the `ConeTwistJoint3D`.

prompt: A cryptographic key (RSA or elliptic-curve).
explain: The CryptoKey class represents a cryptographic key. Keys can be loaded and saved like any other `Resource`.

prompt: Resource filesystem, as the editor sees it.
explain: This object holds information of all resources in the filesystem, their types, etc. Note: This class shouldn't be instantiated directly. Instead, access the singleton using `EditorInterface.get_resource_filesystem()`.

prompt: Base script that can be used to add extension functions to the editor.
explain: Scripts extending this class and implementing its `_run()` method can be executed from the Script Editor's File > Run menu option (or by pressing `Ctrl + Shift + X`) while the editor is running. This is useful for adding custom in-editor functionality to Godot.

prompt: Manages the SceneTree selection in the editor.
explain: This object manages the SceneTree selection in the editor. Note: This class shouldn't be instantiated directly.

prompt: A horizontal scrollbar that goes from left (min) to right (max).
explain: A horizontal scrollbar, typically used to navigate through content that extends beyond the visible width of a control. It is a `Range`-based control and goes from left (min) to right (max).

prompt: A physics joint that restricts the rotation of a 3D physics body around an axis relative to another physics body.
explain: A physics joint that restricts the rotation of a 3D physics body around an axis relative to another physics body. For example, Body A can be a `StaticBody3D` representing a door hinge that a `RigidBody3D` rotates around.

prompt: Singleton that connects the engine with Android plugins to interface with native Android code.
explain: The JNISingleton is implemented only in the Android export. It's used to call methods and connect signals from an Android plugin written in Java or Kotlin.

prompt: Singleton that connects the engine with the browser's JavaScript context in Web export.
explain: The JavaScriptBridge singleton is implemented only in the Web export. It's used to access the browser's JavaScript context.

prompt: Holds collision data from the movement of a `PhysicsBody2D`.
explain: Holds collision data from the movement of a `PhysicsBody2D`, usually from `PhysicsBody2D.move_and_collide()`. When a `PhysicsBody2D` is moved, it stops if it detects a collision with another body.

prompt: Custom logger to receive messages from the internal error/warning stream.
explain: Custom logger to receive messages from the internal error/warning stream. Loggers are registered via `OS.add_logger()`.

prompt: Provides high-performance drawing of a mesh multiple times using GPU instancing.
explain: MultiMesh provides low-level mesh instancing. Drawing thousands of `MeshInstance3D` nodes can be slow, since each object is submitted to the GPU then drawn individually.

prompt: A binary `Semaphore` for synchronization of multiple `Thread`s.
explain: A synchronization mutex (mutual exclusion). This is used to synchronize multiple `Thread`s, and is equivalent to a binary `Semaphore`.

prompt: 3D obstacle used to affect navigation mesh baking or constrain velocities of avoidance controlled agents.
explain: An obstacle needs a navigation map and outline `vertices` defined to work correctly. The outlines can not cross or overlap and are restricted to a plane projection.

prompt: A PBR (Physically Based Rendering) material to be used on 3D objects. Uses an ORM texture.
explain: ORMMaterial3D's properties are inherited from `BaseMaterial3D`. Unlike `StandardMaterial3D`, ORMMaterial3D uses a single texture for ambient occlusion, roughness and metallic maps, known as an ORM texture.

prompt: Placeholder class for a 2-dimensional texture.
explain: - When running the project exported in dedicated server mode, only the texture's dimensions are kept (as they may be relied upon for gameplay purposes or positioning of other elements). This allows reducing the exported PCK's size significantly.

prompt: Compiled shader file in SPIR-V form (used by `RenderingDevice`). Not to be confused with Godot's own `Shader`.
explain: Compiled shader file in SPIR-V form. See also `RDShaderSource`.

prompt: Shader source code (used by `RenderingDevice`).
explain: Shader source code in text form. See also `RDShaderFile`.

prompt: Abstract base class for controls that represent a number within a range.
explain: Range is an abstract base class for controls that represent a number within a range, using a configured `step` and `page` size. See e.g. `ScrollBar` and `Slider` for examples of higher-level nodes using Range.

prompt: Abstract scene buffers object, created for each viewport for which 3D rendering is done.
explain: Abstract scene buffers object, created for each viewport for which 3D rendering is done. It manages any additional buffers used during rendering and will discard buffers when the viewport is resized.

prompt: Abstract render data object, holds scene data related to rendering a single frame of a viewport.
explain: Abstract scene data object, exists for the duration of rendering a single viewport. See also `RenderSceneDataRD`, `RenderData`, and `RenderDataRD`.

prompt: A captured backtrace of a specific script language.
explain: `ScriptBacktrace` holds an already captured backtrace of a specific script language, such as GDScript or C#, which are captured using `Engine.capture_script_backtraces()`. See `ProjectSettings.debug/settings/gdscript/always_track_call_stacks` and `ProjectSettings.debug/settings/gdscript/always_track_local_variables` for ways of controlling the contents of this class.

prompt: A built-in type representing a signal of an `Object`.
explain: `Signal` is a built-in `Variant` type that represents a signal of an `Object` instance. Like all `Variant` types, it can be stored in variables and passed to functions.

prompt: A physics joint that restricts the movement of a 3D physics body along an axis relative to another physics body.
explain: A physics joint that restricts the movement of a 3D physics body along an axis relative to another physics body. For example, Body A could be a `StaticBody3D` representing a piston base, while Body B could be a `RigidBody3D` representing the piston head, moving up and down.

prompt: A 3D raycast that dynamically moves its children near the collision point.
explain: `SpringArm3D` casts a ray or a shape along its Z axis and moves all its direct children to the collision point, with an optional margin. This is useful for 3rd person cameras that move closer to the player when inside a tight space (you may need to exclude the player's collider from the `SpringArm3D`'s collision check).

prompt: Abstract base class for defining stylized boxes for UI elements.
explain: `StyleBox` is an abstract base class for drawing stylized boxes for UI elements. It is used for panels, buttons, `LineEdit` backgrounds, `Tree` backgrounds, etc. and also for testing a transparency mask for pointer signals.

prompt: A `StyleBox` that displays a single line of a given color and thickness.
explain: A `StyleBox` that displays a single line of a given color and thickness. The line can be either horizontal or vertical.

prompt: Base class for 3-dimensional textures.
explain: Base class for `ImageTexture3D` and `CompressedTexture3D`. Cannot be used directly, but contains all the functions necessary for accessing the derived resource types.

prompt: Settings for a single tile in a `TileSet`.
explain: `TileData` object represents a single tile in a `TileSet`. It is usually edited using the tileset editor, but it can be modified at runtime using `TileMapLayer._tile_data_runtime_update()`.

prompt: Contains baked voxel global illumination data for use in a `VoxelGI` node.
explain: `VoxelGIData` contains baked voxel global illumination for use in a `VoxelGI` node. `VoxelGIData` also offers several properties to adjust the final appearance of the global illumination.

prompt: A resource that holds all components of a 2D world, such as a canvas and a physics space.
explain: Class that has everything pertaining to a 2D world: A physics space, a canvas, and a sound space. 2D nodes register their resources into the current 2D world.

prompt: An X509 certificate (e.g. for TLS).
explain: The X509Certificate class represents an X509 certificate. Certificates can be loaded and saved like any other `Resource`.
